69nOcEaHQA.one_liner: Autoregressive skeleton generation with branch-centric tokenization and test-time view augmentation that selects among predictions from rotated meshes.
69nOcEaHQA.problem: Existing skeleton generation approaches struggle to encode branch structures into token sequences and do not use test-time computation effectively.
69nOcEaHQA.method: BranchTokens uses branch-centric tokenization, which places structurally related elements next to each other and encodes connectivity directly in the sequence, giving more compact sequences than BFS-style serialization. View-augmented generation applies axis-aligned rotations to the input mesh, maps predictions back to a common frame, and selects the final skeleton by mesh coverage and consistency across views.
69nOcEaHQA.key_idea: Serialize skeletons branch by branch so related joints and connectivity are adjacent, and choose among predictions from axis-rotated meshes by coverage and cross-view consistency.
69nOcEaHQA.evidence: Experiments on Articulation-XL2.0 against baselines including Auto-Connect, with qualitative results on in-the-wild meshes.
69nOcEaHQA.claimed_gains: Reduces CD-J2B error by 16.9% on Articulation-XL2.0 compared to the strongest baseline, Auto-Connect.

nJsLCIVXUQ.one_liner: Multimodal ReAct agent that investigates whether an image's depicted situation is factually supported, trained with SFT then on-policy self-distillation.
nJsLCIVXUQ.problem: Detecting whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported, and no textual claim is supplied to verify.
nJsLCIVXUQ.method: Defines Image Factuality Assessment and builds EviLens, a benchmark of 10,174 images, plus EviScene, a ReAct agent that interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval and evidence analysis. A compact policy is trained by SFT on reviewed teacher trajectories, then by privileged on-policy self-distillation on verified decisions.
nJsLCIVXUQ.key_idea: The agent refines factual questions through interleaved visual inspection and retrieval, then self-distills its own verified investigation decisions on-policy using privileged information.
nJsLCIVXUQ.evidence: EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and refuted images covering twelve factual error types, evaluated on a 1,527-image test set with a Qwen3.5-9B agent.
nJsLCIVXUQ.claimed_gains: The trained Qwen3.5-9B agent reaches 79.05% balanced accuracy and a 52.26% Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate, improving over the same-backbone base agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points.

7LUU7dOK8Q.one_liner: Benchmark of 470 real livestreams with anchor future-prediction questions and support questions probing perception, interaction, history and causality.
7LUU7dOK8Q.problem: Existing benchmarks underexplore whether MLLMs can anticipate near-future outcomes in interactive livestreams from evolving visual, audio and audience context rather than only comprehend retrospectively.
7LUU7dOK8Q.method: Each video has an anchor question targeting immediate-future prediction plus support questions on perception localization, interaction dynamics, historical understanding and causal attribution. It is built by hierarchical multimodal representation, agentic task formation and automatic verification, with human evaluation of a sampled subset.
7LUU7dOK8Q.key_idea: Pair each future-prediction anchor question with diagnostic support questions to test whether prerequisite capabilities, rather than prediction alone, limit MLLMs.
7LUU7dOK8Q.evidence: 470 real livestreams across six categories and 1,421 questions, with 15 open-source and proprietary MLLMs evaluated across diagnostic dimensions, modalities and languages.
7LUU7dOK8Q.claimed_gains: The strongest model reaches 63.19% accuracy on future prediction in the Full-context setting while achieving 85.07-90.67% across the four diagnostic dimensions.

EEAWDYE7H9.one_liner: ReferFlow grounds multi-step referring expressions by decoupling text-latent trajectory reasoning from parallel coordinate decoding, evaluated on ReferFlow-Bench.
EEAWDYE7H9.problem: REC benchmarks evaluate only final-target localization, leaving the grounding of intermediate visual references in complex queries unexamined.
EEAWDYE7H9.method: Trajectory-level REC gives models an ordered sequence of grounding steps from one complex query. ReferFlow uses Stateful Region Latent Reasoning, with object-indexed continuous latents supervised visually and spatially, and Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding, which recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds.
EEAWDYE7H9.key_idea: Hold each target region as an object-indexed latent state, then decode all coordinate blocks in parallel through geometry-constrained refinement rounds.
EEAWDYE7H9.evidence: ReferFlow-Bench with four trajectory types (Refinement, Shift, Reset, Mixture), where experiments show current models struggle with intermediate references; results for ReferFlow itself are cut off in the abstract.

PFjdmSCPA4.one_liner: PRIM benchmark diagnoses mathematical understanding along four primitives; ABSORB self-distills primitive-guided reasoning into the student model.
PFjdmSCPA4.problem: It is unclear whether LLMs that solve frontier math problems have the structural mathematical understanding underlying their solutions, since solution accuracy masks distinct capability profiles.
PFjdmSCPA4.method: PRIM evaluates mathematical reasoning along four dimensions: Discovery, Generation, Digestion and Execution. ABSORB is a primitive-privileged self-distillation framework that selectively transfers primitive-guided reasoning into the student model.
PFjdmSCPA4.key_idea: Self-distillation in which the teacher view has privileged access to mathematical primitives, selectively transferring primitive-guided reasoning to the student, aimed at discovery-limited failures.
PFjdmSCPA4.evidence: Systematic diagnosis with PRIM across models, a post-training analysis of repairable failures, and experiments on challenging benchmarks across model scales.
PFjdmSCPA4.claimed_gains: ABSORB consistently improves mathematical reasoning over baselines across model scales and challenging benchmarks; no numbers are stated.

natnsNOupN.one_liner: Supervises first-order temporal derivatives of actions in flow-matching action-chunk policies with one extra flow-based loss.
natnsNOupN.problem: Flow-based action-chunk policies treat chunks as unstructured vectors, ignoring physical-time dependencies among actions within a chunk, which can make policy learning ineffective.
natnsNOupN.method: The method additionally supervises the first-order temporal derivatives of actions within a chunk, which the authors show is a special case of path-independent flow matching where generation evolves along denoising time and physical time; it needs only one additional flow-based loss term.
natnsNOupN.key_idea: Add a flow-matching loss on the first-order temporal derivative of the action chunk, so generation evolves jointly along denoising time and physical time.
natnsNOupN.evidence: A broad range of simulation benchmarks and real-robot experiments compared with the base policy.
natnsNOupN.claimed_gains: Consistently improves performance and sample efficiency over the base policy; the abstract is truncated and gives no numbers.

lrpwOygf1b.one_liner: NormGuard adds a hinge penalty on velocity-norm excess over the reference model during flow-matching RL post-training.
lrpwOygf1b.problem: RL post-training of flow generators raises reward but inflates the per-step velocity norm, degrading perceptual quality (contrast, sharpness, white balance) in ways the reward proxy does not capture.
lrpwOygf1b.method: NormGuard is a simple hinge penalty that activates only when the fine-tuned model's velocity norm exceeds the reference model's velocity norm during training; the abstract is truncated after this point.
lrpwOygf1b.key_idea: Penalize velocity-norm excess over the reference model at training time, because inference-time rescaling fails when norm inflation is co-adapted into the weights.
lrpwOygf1b.evidence: Analysis across three post-training methods (NFT, AWM, DPO) measuring norm inflation, plus tests showing inference-time rescaling restores neither reward nor quality and that magnitude rescaling carries no coherent batch-level reward signal.
lrpwOygf1b.claimed_gains: No numeric gain for NormGuard is visible in the truncated abstract; it reports that RL fine-tuning inflates the velocity norm by 5% to 15% and that NormGuard restores quality while preserving reward.

0XysQIdTfc.one_liner: Gives algorithms and lower bounds for finding a consensus lottery with binary queries under bounded adaptivity and parallelism.
0XysQIdTfc.problem: Finding a lottery accepted by every agent, or showing none exists, is costly when feedback is limited in rounds (bounded adaptivity) and in queries per round (bounded parallelism).
0XysQIdTfc.method: Each agent accepts a lottery when its expected utility meets an unknown threshold, and the learner may only ask binary accept/reject queries. The authors determine optimal round and query complexities for learning one agent's acceptable set under bounded parallelism and build consensus algorithms from parallel constraint learning and selective elicitation.
0XysQIdTfc.key_idea: Find consensus without fully learning every agent's constraint, by combining parallel constraint learning with selective elicitation under round and per-round query limits.
0XysQIdTfc.evidence: Theoretical algorithms and lower bounds for arbitrary numbers of agents and alternatives, with tight bounds in several settings for two alternatives.

AV3WQu1TNa.one_liner: ZonoGPT is a zonotope abstract domain with generator reduction and fused Attention/LayerNorm transformations for verifying large transformers.
AV3WQu1TNa.problem: Prior transformer verification is limited to small or restricted models, and precision is hard to maintain across deep models.
AV3WQu1TNa.method: ZonoGPT uses a structured zonotope with a generator reduction mechanism so space complexity is independent of network depth, block-specific fused transformations for Attention and LayerNorm that retain feature relations, and an affine transform for GELU that preserves generator relations.
AV3WQu1TNa.key_idea: Track correlations in a structured zonotope with reduced generators, using fused Attention and LayerNorm transformations and an affine GELU transform that preserve feature and generator relations.
AV3WQu1TNa.evidence: Verification of classifiers trained from scratch with HuggingFace's GPT-2 implementation on text and vision tasks, scaling to GPT-2 Medium (24 blocks, 300M+ parameters).
AV3WQu1TNa.claimed_gains: Verifies 1,339 class-margin instances across text and vision tasks on models up to GPT-2 Medium (24 blocks, 300M+ parameters).

mW8cHYvTE4.one_liner: DDMD-V distills a uniform discrete diffusion video model into one step using on-policy distribution matching plus spatiotemporal adversarial regularization.
mW8cHYvTE4.problem: High-quality discrete diffusion video generation needs repeated refinement steps, and compressing it into one forward pass is hard because tens of thousands of categorical variables must jointly form coherent structure and dynamics without later correction.
mW8cHYvTE4.method: DDMD-V extends on-policy distribution matching to uniform discrete diffusion, using student-induced intermediate states along the teacher's metric-dependent corruption path, and adds spatiotemporal adversarial regularization in the FSQ embedding space for multi-token configurations. Distilled from URSA-1.7B, the student produces a 49-frame 320x512 video of 33,280 discrete tokens in one forward pass.
mW8cHYvTE4.key_idea: Match student and teacher token distributions on student-induced intermediate states along the teacher's corruption path, plus an adversarial signal over multi-token spatiotemporal configurations in FSQ space.
mW8cHYvTE4.evidence: Distillation from URSA-1.7B, evaluated with VBench against the 50-step teacher.
mW8cHYvTE4.claimed_gains: VBench score of 81.78 versus 81.75 for the 50-step teacher, with function evaluations reduced from 100 to one when counting the teacher's conditional and unconditional guidance.

AULx4qdRPs.one_liner: Compiles each session into model-independent latent memory, consolidates it with a recurrent gate, and maps it to backbone-specific LoRA.
AULx4qdRPs.problem: Text-based agent memory depends increasingly on retrieval quality as histories grow, while existing parametric memory supports little cross-session evolution and is tied to a specific backbone.
AULx4qdRPs.method: RPMem is a two-stage architecture: each session is compiled into a model-independent latent memory through forward computation and integrated with retained memory via a task-trained recurrent gate. The consolidated memory is then mapped to backbone-specific LoRA parameters so encoding transfers when the backbone is replaced.
AULx4qdRPs.key_idea: Separate model-independent latent memory consolidation, using a recurrent gate across sessions, from a mapping of that memory to backbone-specific LoRA weights.
AULx4qdRPs.evidence: Three long-term memory benchmarks and five diverse backbones, with ablations of session compilation and cross-session consolidation and analyses of gate dynamics.
AULx4qdRPs.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-8B on PERMA, RPMem reaches 85.52%, outperforming the strongest parametric and text-based baselines by 5.32 and 12.98 percentage points, respectively.

ebI50xHToH.one_liner: Retrieval-augmented forecasting for irregular time series with learned window boundaries, multi-evidence retrieval with MMR, and cross-attention fusion.
ebI50xHToH.problem: Retrieval-augmented forecasting methods assume regular sampling, but on irregular multivariate time series uneven observation density makes fixed windows insufficient or redundant and asynchronous observations complicate retrieval of relevant history.
ebI50xHToH.method: ARISE learns a sample-specific left boundary for each historical window (right boundary fixed) under multiple training objectives, then retrieves history from three relevance views (observation patterns, temporal dynamics, value information) with maximal marginal relevance selection. A memory fusion module uses cross-attention to incorporate retrieved histories and their observed continuations into the predictor.
ebI50xHToH.key_idea: Learn per-sample history window boundaries and retrieve complementary evidence by combining three relevance views with maximal marginal relevance before cross-attention fusion.
ebI50xHToH.evidence: not stated; the experimental section is cut off in the available abstract.

FSwTPYp45Q.one_liner: Path-reversible diffusion bridge that starts from text and interpolates into images, giving a unified bidirectional text-image generator.
FSwTPYp45Q.problem: Existing multimodality translation approaches have semantically meaningless generative paths that limit sampling flexibility, and they are unidirectional, so they cannot invert, for example, image to text.
FSwTPYp45Q.method: BIT starts directly from text and interpolates into images, and is derived through stochastic calculus to give SDE forms friendly to simulation and tractable loss functions that scale to high dimensions. The model is inherently reversible from image to text.
FSwTPYp45Q.key_idea: Bridge text and image distributions directly with a reversible diffusion bridge, so one SDE gives a semantically rich generative path and inversion in both directions.
FSwTPYp45Q.evidence: Theoretical and empirical results compared with denoising diffusion and deterministic flow baselines, in vision-language and natural science tasks.
FSwTPYp45Q.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims competitiveness and often an advantage over denoising diffusion and deterministic flow baselines without numbers.

WaEf3RXP7M.one_liner: Static, training-free linguistic pruning of input text shows which structures LLMs rely on and how pruning interacts with context limits.
WaEf3RXP7M.problem: It is unknown which linguistic structures in the input are load-bearing for LLMs and which can be removed before tokenization, and how this changes when inputs exceed the context window.
WaEf3RXP7M.method: They apply 15 fixed interventions (11 linguistically motivated pruning rules and four random token-deletion controls) to raw text, without LLM-based scoring or task-specific training, and evaluate them unchanged across nine LLMs and six benchmarks.
WaEf3RXP7M.key_idea: Delete linguistically defined structures, such as keeping only each sentence's subject-verb-object core, before tokenization; under context overflow, pruned text lets more evidence fit in the window.
WaEf3RXP7M.evidence: Nine LLMs and six benchmarks including LongBench-v2, plus a controlled budget sweep within one model (Qwen3.5-9B).
WaEf3RXP7M.claimed_gains: Keeping only the subject-verb-object core discards 68% of input tokens on average while retaining 63% of baseline quality; on the longest LongBench-v2 documents the short-document pruning penalty disappears, with the reversal tracking truncation frequency (Spearman rho = 0.93 across models).

iCznVkhSyC.one_liner: VLM agent that actively selects planar views and reorients panoramas via tools, trained with trajectory demonstrations then RL.
iCznVkhSyC.problem: Panoramic projection distortions limit pretrained VLMs' perspective-image abilities, and existing adaptation relies on panoramic QA fine-tuning or predefined planar-view workflows.
iCznVkhSyC.method: PanoAgent jointly learns to select question-relevant panoramic transformations and to answer, using panorama-specific tools to pick local planar views or update the global reference heading. Trajectory demonstrations connect panoramic concepts to observation actions, and RL refines the policy with outcome and geometric feedback.
iCznVkhSyC.key_idea: Let the VLM call tools that render question-relevant planar views or change the global heading, so it reasons with its existing perspective-image skills.
iCznVkhSyC.evidence: Experiments across multiple panoramic benchmarks (names not given in the abstract), compared with other panoramic adaptation methods on accuracy, data efficiency, and inference efficiency.

ei3OmltI4U.one_liner: Trains native 3D texture generation on 2D images only, by turning each image into a plane with patch-wise random rotations.
ei3OmltI4U.problem: Native 3D texture generation is believed to need large-scale, high-quality real 3D assets, which are hard to acquire.
ei3OmltI4U.method: Tex-Zero converts 2D images into 3D training samples by representing each image as a plane and applying patch-wise random rotations and aggregation to build complex geometry. It trains the Tex-Zero VAE and then the Tex-Zero DiT exclusively on this constructed data.
ei3OmltI4U.key_idea: Only fine-grained color matters for texture training, so geometry can be synthesized by rotating and aggregating image patches in 3D instead of taken from real assets.
ei3OmltI4U.evidence: The Tex-Zero VAE, never trained on 3D assets, reconstructs real 3D assets with high quality; the visible abstract names no datasets or benchmarks.

iwLcGvjXHs.one_liner: Wraps each retrieved memory in a stochastic gate with recorded inclusion probability, so one rollout yields per-memory include-versus-exclude credit.
iwLcGvjXHs.problem: Per-memory utilities updated with a shared trajectory return suffer Memory Credit Leakage: co-retrieved irrelevant or harmful memories inherit credit from useful ones and accumulate spurious reinforcement.
iwLcGvjXHs.method: CMPO exposes each memory through a stochastic gate with a recorded inclusion probability, so one rollout contains both included and excluded memories, and reweighting the joint return by these probabilities gives a per-memory comparison that updates the gate (the abstract is cut off here). It suits black-box agents because it randomizes what the agent sees rather than how it acts.
iwLcGvjXHs.key_idea: Randomize memory exposure through gates with known inclusion probabilities and reweight the shared return to estimate each memory's include-versus-exclude contrast from one rollout.
iwLcGvjXHs.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before experiments; no datasets or numbers are shown.

BszXywWSfe.one_liner: Meta-CogGran evolves latent cognitive states over visual evidence and semantic memory, stopping reasoning when the state stabilizes.
BszXywWSfe.problem: CLIP-based MLLMs lose fine-grained visual evidence, DINOv3 lacks high-level semantic abstraction, and existing MLLMs have no mechanism to reconcile perception and semantics during reasoning.
BszXywWSfe.method: Multimodal reasoning is formulated as online latent cognitive state evolution: structured cognitive states are iteratively updated through interaction with visual evidence and semantic memory, and a semantic equilibrium mechanism ends reasoning once the state is stable (abstract text cuts off here).
BszXywWSfe.key_idea: Iteratively update structured latent cognitive states from visual evidence and semantic memory, with a semantic equilibrium criterion deciding when to stop.
BszXywWSfe.evidence: not stated (abstract excerpt ends before the experiments).

ByvDNuombY.one_liner: Merges multiple domain-specialized teachers into one student through meta-learned initialization and an adaptive LoRA rank gate.
ByvDNuombY.problem: In multi-teacher on-policy distillation, stronger teachers can yield a worse merged student (teacher-strengthening paradox) because specialized reasoning reduces student–teacher overlap across domains.
ByvDNuombY.method: GMOPD formulates each base-referenced OPD task as a KL-regularized RL problem and optimizes a meta-objective that learns a shared initialization adapting rapidly to each teacher, plus an adaptive rank gate that activates teacher-relevant LoRA ranks while protecting capabilities needed by the other teachers.
ByvDNuombY.key_idea: Meta-learn a shared initialization for post-adaptation performance on each teacher and gate which LoRA ranks each teacher updates, limiting cross-teacher forgetting.
ByvDNuombY.evidence: Six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, coding, scientific reasoning, instruction following, tool use, and general reasoning, across multiple model scales and up to 20 heterogeneous teachers.
ByvDNuombY.claimed_gains: GMOPD is said to consistently outperform existing merging and distillation methods and to scale to 20 heterogeneous teachers, with no score numbers stated.

wutrzqxrsC.one_liner: World model whose encoder is conditioned on a language task description to extract task-specific state and ignore distractors.
wutrzqxrsC.problem: Encoders in existing world models are non-adaptive, so state representations are distracted by task-irrelevant information in noisy observations.
wutrzqxrsC.method: ConfigWM uses a language description of the current task as a configuration signal that steers how visual embeddings map into a task-specific state space, preserving task-relevant information and suppressing irrelevant variation. Action-conditioned dynamics are then learned in that space for planning.
wutrzqxrsC.key_idea: Condition the visual-embedding-to-state mapping on a language task description, so the same observation yields different task-specific states.
wutrzqxrsC.evidence: Planning and physical-quantity probing evaluations in environments with increasing levels of distraction, against competing world-model methods.
wutrzqxrsC.claimed_gains: ConfigWM outperforms the strongest competing method by 22.3% on average across diverse environments, with a gain of +0.365 Pearson r in physical-quantity probing.

Oc4s2kuySB.one_liner: Multi-agent design-code-review system using physics-simulation feedback to generate simulation-ready articulated 3D assets, plus a benchmark.
Oc4s2kuySB.problem: 3D generation has improved in appearance, but generated objects do not necessarily behave correctly under physical interaction.
Oc4s2kuySB.method: Artisan extends Articraft with a multi-agent pipeline that uses physical simulation feedback to produce collision-free motion, stability under gravity, and accurate mass and material properties. The paper also builds a benchmark covering spatial fidelity, physical plausibility, downstream task performance, and overall quality, using 100 reference assets from ArtVIP and LightWheel, 50 stability prompts, and 50 ABO objects with reference masses.
Oc4s2kuySB.key_idea: Close the generation loop with physical simulation: design, code, and review agents revise asset programs using collision, stability, and mass feedback.
Oc4s2kuySB.evidence: Evaluation of more than 10 representative models on the new benchmark (100 reference assets, 50 stability prompts, 50 ABO objects with reference masses).
Oc4s2kuySB.claimed_gains: Artisan attains competitive spatial fidelity and the lowest collision rates and highest stability rates among the evaluated methods, with no numeric values stated in the abstract.

jbl4qCAXc4.one_liner: A training-free pre-action check detects conflicting sources and passes its result to mediation, improving agents' grounded resolution of source inconsistency.
jbl4qCAXc4.problem: Agents combine user instructions, web observations and internal state that can disagree with no principled basis to prefer one source, and they recognize such conflicts far more often than they act on them.
jbl4qCAXc4.method: The paper defines Source Inconsistency (SOIN) and studies detection and behavior across five models in controlled web-agent settings. A model-agnostic, training-free mechanism explicitly checks for SOIN before action and makes the check result available to downstream mediation.
jbl4qCAXc4.key_idea: Insert an explicit source-inconsistency check before action and expose its full result to decision-time mediation, without any training.
jbl4qCAXc4.evidence: Five models in controlled web-agent settings, measuring explicit detection, spontaneous resolution and grounded task success on conflict and no-conflict cases.
jbl4qCAXc4.claimed_gains: Explicit SOIN detection reaches up to 100.00%; with the full checking result, grounded task success in conflict cases rises to 62.51-100.00%, reaching 99.13-100.00% for four of the five models.

GdGQabLUmD.one_liner: Feed-forward view synthesis that predicts 3D points with features and aggregates them per target ray via ray-to-point attention.
GdGQabLUmD.problem: 3DGS-based feed-forward methods need many primitives for fine detail, while geometry-free methods struggle to keep geometric consistency under unseen camera transformations.
GdGQabLUmD.method: PointWeave predicts 3D points with appearance features from input views, aggregates their features for each target ray with learned ray-to-point attention, combines the feature map with colors retrieved from the input views through inferred geometry, and decodes the target image.
GdGQabLUmD.key_idea: Use explicit 3D points as the interface between geometry and learned appearance, with each target ray attending to points and to colors reprojected from the input views.
GdGQabLUmD.evidence: RealEstate10K, with zero-shot transfer to ACID, DL3DV, ScanNet++ and DTU, and tests under camera roll, field-of-view, pixel-aspect and world-scale changes.
GdGQabLUmD.claimed_gains: 31.38 dB PSNR with 8,192 points on RealEstate10K, 1.6 dB above recent 3DGS-based methods with fewer primitives; up to 4x faster rendering than geometry-free methods at matched performance; zero-shot gains of 0.54 to 2.02 dB PSNR.

1FAprBGimt.one_liner: Releases a dataset of 3,421 human egocentric demonstrations with verified step rationales and a closed-loop benchmark for embodied reasoning.
1FAprBGimt.problem: Embodied VLM agents in a closed loop revisit searched views, lose targets that leave the frame and switch referents, and existing demonstrations record views and actions but not the observations behind each action.
1FAprBGimt.method: EmbRACE collects human demonstrations in photorealistic Unreal Engine environments, each step carrying a rationale verified against the frames, plus a benchmark of 686 tasks in 7 held-out environments scored on final position and door and object states.
1FAprBGimt.key_idea: Attach to every demonstration step a frame-verified rationale stating what the action was based on, and evaluate models in a closed loop on tasks that need earlier observations.
1FAprBGimt.evidence: 3,421 demonstrations (48,264 steps) across indoor and outdoor environments, a 686-task benchmark, frontier models evaluated, and four open models of 2B to 9B parameters fine-tuned.
1FAprBGimt.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning four open models of 2B to 9B parameters raises overall scores from 3% to 8% up to 57% to 68%; frontier models score below half when the target must be searched for or returned to.

rZc9uOU2OO.one_liner: Replaces token-level logit matching in on-policy distillation with chunk-level supervision from Monte Carlo rollouts and a peak-entropy scheduler.
rZc9uOU2OO.problem: Standard on-policy distillation needs teacher token logits, which excludes proprietary teachers, and the token-level logit signal is brittle and can amplify repetition loops.
rZc9uOU2OO.method: OmniOPD approximates the teacher's preferences with Monte Carlo rollouts scored by a continuous semantic similarity over multi-token chunks, and a peak-entropy scheduler applies supervision only at the student's high-uncertainty reasoning forks.
rZc9uOU2OO.key_idea: Score multi-token chunks by semantic similarity to teacher preferences via Monte Carlo rollouts, and audit the student only at peak-entropy positions, avoiding teacher logits.
rZc9uOU2OO.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and competitive programming benchmarks, compared with SFT and standard white-box on-policy distillation.
rZc9uOU2OO.claimed_gains: Up to +45.31% relative over SFT on math and up to +28.64% over standard white-box OPD on mathematical reasoning.

NmcA9Wzeu7.one_liner: Repairs self-intersections in rigged mesh animations by alternating mesh-space proxy repair with rig-space pose adaptation.
NmcA9Wzeu7.problem: Motion sequences from generation models often contain surface collisions and self-intersections, and fixing them while preserving the original spatiotemporal motion is under-explored.
NmcA9Wzeu7.method: Proxyboros alternates mesh-space repair with rig-space pose adaptation. Mesh-Space Proxy Exploration extracts intermediate geometric proxies that capture local repair tendencies, and Proxy-Guided Pose Adaptation folds them into a temporally coupled skeletal trajectory using surface-aware guidance.
NmcA9Wzeu7.key_idea: Use intermediate mesh-space repair proxies, before independent repairs settle into inconsistent static fixes, to guide a temporally coupled skeletal trajectory.
NmcA9Wzeu7.evidence: SMPL-H sequences and diverse non-SMPL rigged models, compared with prior methods on repair quality, pose preservation and motion (the abstract is cut off).
NmcA9Wzeu7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports favorable overall performance without numbers).

5fhvojTixh.one_liner: Training-free gate that discards unreliable geometric priors in feed-forward 3D reconstruction using prior-prediction residual and attention entropy.
5fhvojTixh.problem: Prior-conditioned feed-forward reconstruction models can produce worse results than image-only reconstruction when camera, pose or depth priors are inaccurate or corrupted.
5fhvojTixh.method: Gate3R combines the residual between each prior and the model's prediction with the frozen model's attention entropy to decide whether the prior is usable, and falls back to image-only reconstruction otherwise.
5fhvojTixh.key_idea: Gate each geometric prior at test time by combining its residual against the prediction with the frozen model's attention entropy.
5fhvojTixh.evidence: Two prior-conditioned models, Pow3R and MapAnything, across six datasets in single-prior and multi-prior settings, against always keeping and always discarding priors.
5fhvojTixh.claimed_gains: Outperforms always keeping and always discarding priors in most single-prior settings and all multi-prior settings across six datasets; no numeric gains stated.

Xw98wKuymD.one_liner: Benchmark of 20,648 Chinese Sign Language sequences with four aligned versions that make video-to-humanoid retargeting errors traceable.
Xw98wKuymD.problem: Errors from fitting, human-motion repair, retargeting, robot geometry repair and control are hard to separate from the final humanoid signing trajectory alone.
Xw98wKuymD.method: HumanoidCSL-20K gives each sentence-level sequence four aligned versions (source, repaired human motion, direct robot reference, geometry-repaired robot reference), with local human-motion repair, full-robot geometry repair and cross-representation provenance. A sign-specific kinematic-reference protocol scores handshape, location, palm orientation and inter-hand relation.
Xw98wKuymD.key_idea: Store every transformation stage as a separate aligned version with provenance so errors can be attributed to fitting, repair, retargeting or control.
Xw98wKuymD.evidence: Full-corpus paired evaluations of motion continuity, content preservation, robot feasibility and physical execution, plus control experiments separating reference learnability from curriculum effects.
Xw98wKuymD.claimed_gains: Repair yields fewer abnormal arm and hand steps and less inter-hand and hand-body penetration; no numbers stated.

vv9hjQ7FwW.one_liner: Connects intermediate native visual representations of pretrained MLLMs directly to the language model for AI-generated image detection.
vv9hjQ7FwW.problem: MLLM-based AI-generated image detection needs low-level forensic evidence, but that information becomes less accessible along the standard vision-language pathway.
vv9hjQ7FwW.method: Native Forensic Connection (NFC) routes intermediate visual representations, where low-level forensic information is already discriminative, directly to the language model without adapting the vision encoder. The authors also build SemClean-Bench by reverse semantic filtering.
vv9hjQ7FwW.key_idea: Feed intermediate-layer native visual features that retain forensic cues directly into the language model, bypassing the standard vision-language pathway that dilutes them.
vv9hjQ7FwW.evidence: Diverse AIGI benchmarks plus SemClean-Bench, which evaluates detection when salient semantic anomalies are less frequent.
vv9hjQ7FwW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports strong and generalizable performance without numbers).

48xAUsPMuo.one_liner: Dual-stream vision-language model that takes polarimetric physical parameters alongside RGB, trained in two stages on a polarization VQA set.
48xAUsPMuo.problem: VLMs struggle with optical ambiguities such as reflections and transparent objects because standard RGB inputs lack the needed physical information.
48xAUsPMuo.method: PolarVLM uses a dual-stream architecture and a progressive two-stage training strategy to integrate polarimetric parameters into a VLM. The authors also build PolarVQA, a benchmark of 75K physics-grounded instruction-tuning pairs for reflective and transparent scenes.
48xAUsPMuo.key_idea: Add a second stream carrying polarimetric parameters to a VLM and train progressively so physical cues are not misinterpreted while general visual ability is retained.
48xAUsPMuo.evidence: Five evaluation tasks on PolarVQA (75K pairs) compared with an RGB baseline.
48xAUsPMuo.claimed_gains: Surpasses the RGB baseline by 25.4% overall across five evaluation tasks, with gains of 26.6% in reflection recognition and 34.0% in glass counting.

L9snLZDjdx.one_liner: Decision-level RL that compares commit versus re-examine continuations from the same search state to credit verdict tokens.
L9snLZDjdx.problem: Prompting, demonstrations, and outcome-based RL can encourage re-examination in visual search but do not supervise whether another observation is beneficial at a particular search state.
L9snLZDjdx.method: CARE compares paired continuations under commit and re-examine verdicts from the same state, uses their cost-aware return difference as the counterfactual value of an extra observation, and assigns it only to the verdict tokens. The authors also build RESEE, a benchmark of 3,227 trajectories and 8,827 commit-or-re-examine decisions with counterfactual adjudication.
L9snLZDjdx.key_idea: Estimate the counterfactual value of another observation from paired commit and re-examine continuations, and assign that credit only to the verdict tokens.
L9snLZDjdx.evidence: The RESEE benchmark with 3,227 visual-search trajectories and 8,827 decisions; experiments compare CARE with GRPO across two backbones and on six unseen settings (noun truncated in the abstract).

Hak4lWkqCD.one_liner: Post-trains an open 9B multimodal LLM on solver-verified data to write optimization formulations and solver code from text and images.
Hak4lWkqCD.problem: Existing optimization-modeling methods assume text-only problem specifications, and existing multimodal benchmarks show a gap between open and proprietary MLLMs but provide no training data or post-training methods.
Hak4lWkqCD.method: MLLM4OR is trained first with supervised fine-tuning to connect text-image evidence to formulations and solver code (later training stages are truncated in the abstract), using the MLLM4OR-Corpus of 22,107 solver-verified instances split into training, development, and test subsets.
Hak4lWkqCD.key_idea: Supervise a compact open MLLM on solver-verified text-image problems so it emits mathematical formulations and runnable solver code.
Hak4lWkqCD.evidence: An in-domain test split of MLLM4OR-Corpus and external evaluation on MM-OptBench and LLM4OR-VL, which has 878 multimodal problems reconstructed from eight text-only optimization benchmarks.

OTn4LX7KlD.one_liner: Online clustering of linear bandits where agents share data once locally certified, without knowing arrival frequencies.
OTn4LX7KlD.problem: Prior clustering-of-bandits analyses tie collaboration benefits to identifying the full cluster structure, so rarely observed agents delay benefits even for agents whose preferences are already estimated accurately.
OTn4LX7KlD.method: In LC-CLUB each agent first learns from its own observations and, once its estimate is accurate enough to be certified, starts sharing with certified agents in the same cluster. The regret analysis separates each agent's pre-certification interactions from its later cluster-level learning.
OTn4LX7KlD.key_idea: Let an agent pool data with certified same-cluster agents as soon as its own estimate is certified, before the global clusters are identified.
OTn4LX7KlD.evidence: Regret analysis under heterogeneous agent arrivals and smoothed adversarial contexts (per the keywords); the abstract is truncated before any experiments.

m9IhP9Hkec.one_liner: Studies online fair division of indivisible goods under item-level and bundle-level upgrade recourse and the maximin-share factors achievable.
m9IhP9Hkec.problem: In online fair division with irrevocable assignments no algorithm guarantees any positive fraction of the maximin share, while unrestricted reassignment can take value away from agents who already hold goods.
m9IhP9Hkec.method: The paper allows reassignment only if every affected agent ends at least as well off, either per item (item-level upgrades) or in total value (bundle-level upgrades), and analyzes the achievable MMS factors, including fixed picking sequences for the item-level case.
m9IhP9Hkec.key_idea: Restrict reassignments to upgrades, so each agent keeps or replaces each good with one valued at least as much, or keeps total value under bundle-level upgrades.
m9IhP9Hkec.evidence: Theoretical analysis only as stated: bounds for item-level upgrades and constructions for bundle-level upgrades, with the final result truncated in the abstract.
m9IhP9Hkec.claimed_gains: For item-level upgrades the optimal MMS factor is essentially 1/H_n, about 1/ln n; bundle-level upgrades achieve exact MMS for two agents and more than half of MMS for any number of agents.

IOxd2T3tfl.one_liner: VLA model that injects 3D geometric representations into its VLM and conditions the action expert on generated spatial reasoning.
IOxd2T3tfl.problem: VLA models inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained VLMs but struggle to develop 3D spatial understanding and use it to guide action generation.
IOxd2T3tfl.method: SpaVLA adds a 3D-aware module that incorporates geometric representations into the VLM backbone, trains on ManiSpatial-565K (robot manipulation data paired with 3D spatial QA annotations) with a progressive training strategy, and conditions the action expert on the VLM's spatial reasoning.
IOxd2T3tfl.key_idea: Make 3D spatial understanding explicit in the VLM through geometry features and spatial QA supervision, then condition the action expert on that reasoning.
IOxd2T3tfl.evidence: MMSI-Bench and MindCube for spatial understanding, manipulation evaluation (list truncated), and SimplerEnv-Spatial, a new 20-task benchmark for spatial referring and reasoning.
IOxd2T3tfl.claimed_gains: 48.6% on MMSI-Bench and 95.6% on MindCube, with manipulation success rates of 84.4% on Google (the rest is truncated in the abstract).

LbGqNEnzW9.one_liner: Applies latent supervision only at the last-layer state during a 10-step crossfade into token-level on-policy distillation.
LbGqNEnzW9.problem: Latent on-policy distillation methods such as OPRD show early gain then late collapse, and the best-aligned model performs worst, likely because depth-paired layers play different roles in teacher and student.
LbGqNEnzW9.method: LastOPD applies the latent signal only at the last-layer state, the common interface both LM heads read, and only during a 10-step crossfade into token-level OPD, handing the student to token-level supervision before collapse.
LbGqNEnzW9.key_idea: Align only last-layer states, which both LM heads read, and fade that latent loss out into token-level distillation within ten steps.
LbGqNEnzW9.evidence: Distilling Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B into Qwen3-1.7B-Base, where latent supervision alone lifts MATH-500 accuracy from 25 to 46 in 10 steps and then falls to 11; the LastOPD results are truncated.
LbGqNEnzW9.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is truncated before the LastOPD results)

9G6X8auUdk.one_liner: Continual post-training that distills each new-task expert into one base-sized checkpoint, using per-task generators to relabel prior tasks.
9G6X8auUdk.problem: Foundation models should learn new tasks after deployment without forgetting or growing; self-distillation keeps size fixed but is limited by the model's own capabilities, while expert routing grows the deployed model with every task.
9G6X8auUdk.method: At each stage ReCap trains an expert on the new task and distills it into a single base-sized checkpoint. For prior tasks, a small per-task generator reconstructs input embeddings that the corresponding frozen expert relabels, giving stable distillation targets.
9G6X8auUdk.key_idea: Recover frozen experts' behavior without deploying them by relabeling generator-reconstructed input embeddings with each frozen expert as distillation targets.
9G6X8auUdk.evidence: CoIN and UCIT-O task sequences, six held-out benchmarks, and Qwen and Llama models from 1B to 7B on vision-language and text-only task sequences.
9G6X8auUdk.claimed_gains: 78.0% on CoIN and 75.5% on UCIT-O average accuracy, matching or outperforming the strongest expert-routing baselines, and +2.1 points average over the base model across six held-out benchmarks.

JZjk6rSfFe.one_liner: Scrubber that replaces each detected PII with a realistic synthetic identity of the same type instead of removing it.
JZjk6rSfFe.problem: Imperfect PII scrubbers leave a small amount of real PII that the model memorizes, so missed PII becomes more vulnerable than with no scrubbing, and current rewriting tools produce repetitive or malformed text.
JZjk6rSfFe.method: PII-RADAR replaces each detected PII with a realistic one of the same type, drawn from a pool of validated synthetic identities and formatted to match the original document.
JZjk6rSfFe.key_idea: Substitute detected PII with validated synthetic identities of the same type, avoiding the sparsity of real PII that removal leaves for the model to memorize.
JZjk6rSfFe.evidence: Leakage measured across seven scrubbers (per the TL;DR), showing leakage rises with detection rate; the PII-RADAR results are truncated in the abstract.

YGDYGf6pa2.one_liner: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation that supervises a student with routed specialists' hidden states and token predictions.
YGDYGf6pa2.problem: Existing multi-teacher on-policy distillation for LLMs transfers only what specialists predict through output distributions, not the hidden-state representations used to compute them.
YGDYGf6pa2.method: Latent-MOPD selects late-layer targets according to the teacher-student relationship, bridges unequal hidden widths with a shared projection, groups updates by domain, and gradually shifts each teacher's supervision from hidden states to token predictions using the same routed specialist for both channels.
YGDYGf6pa2.key_idea: Supervise the student with routed specialists' late-layer hidden states and gradually shift to token-level supervision, with domain-grouped updates.
YGDYGf6pa2.evidence: Same-family and cross-family teacher settings on nine benchmarks across math, code, and logic against token-only, representation-only, and uniform-averaging baselines, plus an all-layer representation-only control.
YGDYGf6pa2.claimed_gains: Outperforms token-only, representation-only, and uniform-averaging baselines on all nine benchmarks in the same-family setting and surpasses the per-benchmark best teacher on a majority of benchmarks; no numeric margins stated.

xEAKzV23yi.one_liner: Mixture-of-Transformers world model jointly generating video, semantic voxels, and camera poses with a spatial rotary encoding.
xEAKzV23yi.problem: Interactive world models struggle to keep spatial consistency over long rollouts, and misalignment between 2D pixels and 3D geometry features limits information exchange between video and explicit 3D state.
xEAKzV23yi.method: MoTWorld represents images, voxels, and camera parameters as separate streams with modality-specific weights and shared attention, and uses a spatial rotary positional encoding built from camera geometry and predicted depth to place both modalities in a common 3D coordinate system. Changing which streams are observed or generated lets one model do image-to-voxel reconstruction, voxel-to-image rendering, and action-conditioned rollout.
xEAKzV23yi.key_idea: Place image and voxel tokens in one 3D coordinate system via a camera-geometry rotary encoding so shared attention can establish cross-modal correspondence.
xEAKzV23yi.evidence: Two Minecraft-style evaluation sets with exact 3D ground truth, testing single-image voxel reconstruction and video quality over 600-frame rollouts.

mw8CIwaxPZ.one_liner: Two-stage robot policy fine-tuning that aligns target-demo representations to retrieved pre-training demos and constrains their drift.
mw8CIwaxPZ.problem: Directly fine-tuning a pretrained robot policy such as a VLA on a few demonstrations can distort pretrained representations and weaken out-of-distribution generalization.
mw8CIwaxPZ.method: RARA first retrieves pre-training demonstrations with similar task intent and motion and aligns the policy's representations of target demonstrations with the pretrained representations of the retrieved ones. It then fine-tunes on the target demonstrations while limiting how much its representations of the retrieved demonstrations change.
mw8CIwaxPZ.key_idea: Use retrieved pre-training demonstrations as anchors: align target representations to them before action learning, then limit representation change on them during fine-tuning.
mw8CIwaxPZ.evidence: Diffusion Policy and GR00T on 13 tasks in RoboTwin and RoboCasa, plus a real robot.
mw8CIwaxPZ.claimed_gains: Improves average fine-tuning success by 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution, and outperforms all (comparison list truncated).

cihGLJh9f4.one_liner: Fine-tunes an LLM to emit a token window per forward pass from one shared Gaussian latent, fit by conditional IMLE.
cihGLJh9f4.problem: Autoregressive models emit one token per forward pass so latency grows with output length, and tokens written in the same pass cannot see one another; existing fixes use a draft model, verifier, or extra passes.
cihGLJh9f4.method: IMLE-LLM adds a small latent projection to a pretrained decoder-only transformer so all positions in a window share one Gaussian latent, letting a single pass commit mutually dependent tokens. It is fit with conditional implicit maximum likelihood estimation, which needs no network to infer the latent.
cihGLJh9f4.key_idea: A shared Gaussian latent across a window's positions couples tokens generated in one pass, trained with conditional IMLE rather than an inference network.
cihGLJh9f4.evidence: Built on Qwen3-8B and compared with one-token decoding and an autoregressive fine-tune.
cihGLJh9f4.claimed_gains: Mean speed-up of 3.39x over one-token decoding (up to 3.4x wall-clock per the TL;DR) while keeping most of the accuracy of an autoregressive fine-tune.

fJXPPgqOiB.one_liner: Shows finite activations cannot certify local stability and derives secant-frame Jacobian recovery certificates and a regularizer, SFR.
fJXPPgqOiB.problem: The geometry of finitely observed embeddings does not determine local stability of the representation map: identical activations can correspond to arbitrarily large local sensitivity, and queries leave directions outside their span unidentified.
fJXPPgqOiB.method: Using a classical anchored interpolation operator, the paper recovers the Jacobian restricted to the covered subspace up to a curvature-conditioning error that depends on an independently provided local smoothness bound, yielding two-sided sensitivity estimates, displacement bounds, and a prediction-invariance condition. This leads to Secant-Frame Regularization (SFR), an input-Jacobian-free objective that targets the largest reconstructed logit response.
fJXPPgqOiB.key_idea: Reconstruct the Jacobian on the subspace spanned by perturbation queries via anchored interpolation, and regularize its largest logit response without computing input Jacobians.
fJXPPgqOiB.evidence: A 1D construction meeting the recovery bound for a one-sided endpoint query, and CIFAR-10 experiments comparing SFR with matched-query pairwise consistency on covered transformations.

k6IVm6JQzu.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,200 questions testing whether multimodal agent memory preserves pixel-level visual detail and tracks changing visual states.
k6IVm6JQzu.problem: Existing multimodal memory evaluations let image questions be answered from captions or text and rarely cover visual states that change over time.
k6IVm6JQzu.method: MemEye organizes questions along two axes, scene-level to pixel-level visual evidence and single-evidence retrieval to reasoning over changing states, with 100 questions per taxonomy cell across eight life-scenario tasks and validation gates for answerability, shortcut resistance, visual necessity, and reasoning structure.
k6IVm6JQzu.key_idea: Build questions that require the original visual evidence, graded by visual detail level and by whether memory evolves, and filter them with ablation-driven validation gates.
k6IVm6JQzu.evidence: 13 memory methods evaluated across four VLM backbones on 1,200 questions in eight life-scenario tasks.

splSFnPJdt.one_liner: Turns one black-box action into statistical evidence about hidden information using a regret-to-evidence test with a public geometric contract.
splSFnPJdt.problem: Decision quality does not show what a released action reveals about the information that shaped it, and if the null and alternative induce the same action law, no action-only test can have power above its Type-I error.
splSFnPJdt.method: FanOpt fixes a source-independent baseline and a public distance before private observations arrive; under the null, low regret keeps the action near the baseline, while under a structured alternative low regret forces it away, so a fixed distance threshold yields a test.
splSFnPJdt.key_idea: Low regret keeps the action near a public baseline under the null but forces it away under an information-dependent alternative, so a fixed distance threshold becomes a test.
splSFnPJdt.evidence: Finite-sample Type I and Type II error bounds, an explicit certified regret radius, a marginal-load bound, and certificates for 2-factors, a stated spanning-tree policy, and matching.

O9NsQ0QEnr.one_liner: Multi-stage agentic system that compiles LEGO models and brick-by-brick instructions through a construction SDK with a Meta-Reviewer agent.
O9NsQ0QEnr.problem: LEGO model generation needs physical support per brick and unblocked placement, and training an expert LLM requires generating extremely long context over all brick connections.
O9NsQ0QEnr.method: DailyBrick reduces the problem to writing a program that builds the LEGO model step by step, using role-based multi-stage prompts, a versioned construction SDK that compiles decisions from semantic subparts to individual bricks into canonical operations, and an external Meta-Reviewer agent that replays and verifies the package, traces failures to stages, and routes them to bounded repairs.
O9NsQ0QEnr.key_idea: Have LLM agents write a program that builds the model through a construction SDK, with a reviewer agent replaying the build to localize failures to a stage.
O9NsQ0QEnr.evidence: Experiments against recent agentic systems and downstream robot manipulation on model assembly from instructions and brick sets (details truncated).

b6sqtFuUwe.one_liner: Separates rollout generation from retention: a carrier learns from verified successes across batches and guides the actor via on-policy distillation.
b6sqtFuUwe.problem: GRPO-style response weighting uses only current-batch gradients and can miss useful directions revealed by earlier successful responses.
b6sqtFuUwe.method: An acting policy generates responses while a non-acting carrier learns from verified successes across batches; the actor reads the carrier on its own sampled prefixes through on-policy distillation, with a control-variate write and pre-write reading for stability.
b6sqtFuUwe.key_idea: A separate carrier accumulates verified successes across batches, and the actor reads its token log-ratios on its own prefixes as token-level credit without replaying source responses.
b6sqtFuUwe.evidence: Qwen3-8B on SciKnowEval compared with SDPO and GRPO, a theoretical comparison in a binary-verifier family at a fixed actor, and a test on 27 rarely solved Physics prompts.
b6sqtFuUwe.claimed_gains: 76.22 average maximum Avg@16 on SciKnowEval, 3.29 and 5.17 percentage points above reported SDPO and GRPO, leading in three of four domains, and 29.40 points above GRPO at step 200 on 27 Physics prompts.

JJDRW70mp0.one_liner: Maps sparse option quotes to increment densities of an exponential additive martingale, giving statically arbitrage-free IV surfaces by construction.
JJDRW70mp0.problem: Reconstructing a continuous implied volatility surface from a small number of option quotes, for option pricing and risk management, while satisfying static no-arbitrage conditions.
JJDRW70mp0.method: ADDMART maps sparse quotes to non-negative increment densities of an exponential additive martingale, from which valid risk-neutral marginals and IVs are recovered, building the no-arbitrage structure into the architecture rather than the learning objective.
JJDRW70mp0.key_idea: Parameterize the surface through martingale increment densities so static no-arbitrage holds architecturally instead of through a regularization penalty.
JJDRW70mp0.evidence: Ten real-option datasets, with downstream estimation of VaR, CVaR, and crash probabilities.

iOT5HsWklm.one_liner: Jointly generates humanoid and object motion from text and object-level spatial constraints, with a shared interaction field for execution.
iOT5HsWklm.problem: Collecting humanoid loco-manipulation data via teleoperation or motion capture is costly, and existing generative approaches do not model or control the manipulated object.
iOT5HsWklm.method: CoLM jointly generates humanoid and object motion from a text description, object geometry, and initial states, with spatial control from a target object pose to a full trajectory, and executes it with a motion tracking policy. Training data comes from retargeting human-object interaction data to the humanoid with contact-guided refinement, and an interaction field, a dense representation of humanoid-object spatial relations, serves as a shared objective for generation and execution.
iOT5HsWklm.key_idea: A dense interaction field of humanoid-object spatial relations acts as one shared objective across motion generation and tracking-policy execution.
iOT5HsWklm.evidence: A dataset built by retargeting existing human-object interaction data with contact-guided refinement, and experiments against baselines on motion quality and spatial-constraint satisfaction (details truncated).

jpdVMTIyh6.one_liner: Decouples visible-material estimation, surface alignment and 3D completion to texture meshes from one image with PBR materials.
jpdVMTIyh6.problem: Existing single-image 3D texturing methods introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or lose fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning.
jpdVMTIyh6.method: An MLLM-based image editing model predicts lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view; these are projected onto the visible surface and encoded by a pretrained material VAE encoder into observation latents. An interleaved flow transformer keeps them as fixed read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents.
jpdVMTIyh6.key_idea: Encode visible PBR maps into the 3D generator's own latent space as fixed read-only anchors, then alternate unobserved-region and full-surface latent updates.
jpdVMTIyh6.evidence: Trained solely on public datasets; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not name benchmarks or baselines.

0t6zduj8Lg.one_liner: Transfers egocentric human video to robot policies via interaction-centric latent actions with spectral guidance.
0t6zduj8Lg.problem: Latent actions inferred by reconstructing consecutive frames are dominated by nuisance motion such as ego-camera motion, and human and robot interactions differ in temporal dynamics, which makes transfer to robot policies hard.
0t6zduj8Lg.method: WING uses an interaction-motion decoupling mechanism that separates interaction-relevant signals from task-irrelevant motion and distills the interaction-centric components into latent actions. A second component, motivated by an observation about cross-embodiment task dynamics, adds spectral guidance (details are cut off in the supplied abstract).
0t6zduj8Lg.key_idea: Decouple interaction-relevant signals from ego-camera motion, distill only the interaction-centric components into latent actions, and guide them with spectral information.
0t6zduj8Lg.evidence: Not stated in the supplied (truncated) abstract; the setting is egocentric human video transferred to robot policies.

UZfJEzWaom.one_liner: Pixel diffusion transformer using asymmetric long skips and adaGLU decoder blocks, scaling to 1.6B parameters.
UZfJEzWaom.problem: Training pixel diffusion models relies on ad hoc recipes and architecture designs and is sensitive to hyper-parameter choices.
UZfJEzWaom.method: Replaces the U-Net long skip with asymmetric long skips that pass fine-grained information from input embeddings to decoder layers, and adds adaGLU, a SwiGLU-like MLP block in decoder layers that adaptively filters the embeddings before they are added to main-branch features.
UZfJEzWaom.key_idea: Route input embeddings to decoder layers through asymmetric long skips filtered by an adaptive SwiGLU-like block, instead of a linear skip-plus-main combination.
UZfJEzWaom.evidence: Trained from scratch and scaled from small baselines up to 1.6B parameters on ImageNet-256 and -512, with text-to-image generation as evidence of multimodal input support.
UZfJEzWaom.claimed_gains: 1.62 FID on ImageNet-256 and 1.70 FID on ImageNet-512, with competitive text-to-image performance.

f1MMCsXnVb.one_liner: Represents camera trajectories as videos of projected colored 3D landmarks, jointly modeled with video in one diffusion transformer.
f1MMCsXnVb.problem: Camera-controlled video generation needs a representation that relates geometric motion to visual dynamics without reconstructing the underlying scene.
f1MMCsXnVb.method: Camera motion is encoded as evolving projections of colored landmarks in a synthetic 3D reference structure, with color identity separated from spatial placement and a spatial codebook adapting the structure's scale and layout within a limited identity budget. A shared video diffusion transformer models video and visual pose for camera-controlled generation and video-conditioned pose recovery.
f1MMCsXnVb.key_idea: Encode camera pose as a rendered video of color-coded landmarks whose spatial layout is adapted by a codebook within a fixed color-identity budget.
f1MMCsXnVb.evidence: Controlled comparisons against alternative representations, plus evaluation on DL3DV and Tanks and Temples (results are cut off in the supplied abstract).
f1MMCsXnVb.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports improved camera control and pose recovery over alternative representations without numbers.

jxhrRAeDHM.one_liner: Rule-decomposed audio-language reasoning reward model that verifies semantic and paralinguistic criteria to drive RL for spoken dialogue.
jxhrRAeDHM.problem: Audio-language reward models collapse semantic and paralinguistic factors into one opaque holistic score, which makes failures hard to interpret and gives weak learning signals for RL on spoken dialogue models.
jxhrRAeDHM.method: RubriVox-Verifier decomposes spoken-response evaluation into semantic and paralinguistic critic rules, routes each rule to the proper evidence source, and aggregates the verified rule-level judgments into a scalar reward used for downstream RL.
jxhrRAeDHM.key_idea: Score a spoken response by verifying separate semantic and paralinguistic rules against rule-specific evidence, then aggregate the verdicts into one reward.
jxhrRAeDHM.evidence: Downstream RL experiments on spoken dialogue models and a demo page; specific benchmarks and models are not stated.

rLVPdTwORn.one_liner: Contrastive training on target-versus-distractor UI elements, plus inference-time candidate revisiting, improves GUI grounding.
rLVPdTwORn.problem: GUI grounding models often click non-target interface elements rather than the background, and different models repeatedly select the same distractors.
rLVPdTwORn.method: ConClick trains on ConClick-Data, 4,292 target-distractor pairs, with complementary listwise ranking and pairwise margin objectives. ReClick is an inference-time strategy that revisits promising regions and compares predictions across competing candidates.
rLVPdTwORn.key_idea: Teach the model to separate the target element from plausible distractors using listwise ranking and pairwise margin losses on hard target-distractor pairs.
rLVPdTwORn.evidence: Error analysis of 10 grounding models across five datasets; evaluation of Qwen3-VL-8B on ScreenSpot-Pro, MMBench-GUI L2 and OSWorld-G.
rLVPdTwORn.claimed_gains: Qwen3-VL-8B improves from 54.71% to 66.03% on ScreenSpot-Pro, from 83.72% to 86.28% on MMBench-GUI L2 and from 63.33% to 70.20% on OSWorld-G, and ReClick adds 2.96 percentage points on average.

l1eFFyZcZg.one_liner: Guides MMDiT sampling by suppressing image-to-text feedback in joint attention, without training.
l1eFFyZcZg.problem: In MMDiTs, image-to-text feedback through joint attention can preserve objects and attributes already in the evolving image, including errors, rather than correct deviations from the prompt.
l1eFFyZcZg.method: Semantic Feedback Guidance (SFG) guides away from an auxiliary branch that strengthens image-to-text feedback and weakens text-to-image conditioning; the in-place variant iSFG directly suppresses the feedback and strengthens text-to-image conditioning with no extra model evaluations. The SFG branch runs only during the first 20% of image sampling steps.
l1eFFyZcZg.key_idea: Steer sampling away from an auxiliary branch that amplifies image-to-text feedback, applied only during the first 20% of image sampling steps.
l1eFFyZcZg.evidence: Intervention studies (transplanting image-to-text messages, matched-strength suppression) and experiments across three image-generation backbones including FLUX and SD3.5M; keywords also list text-to-video.
l1eFFyZcZg.claimed_gains: On FLUX, adding SFG to CFG raises GenEval from 0.6661 to 0.7479; on SD3.5M, iSFG adds +1.33 HPSv2.1 over CFG.

brgf3Wa1iv.one_liner: Shows one-pixel screenshot size changes flip GUI grounding clicks via dynamic-resolution preprocessing transition points.
brgf3Wa1iv.problem: Changing a screenshot dimension by a single pixel can alter which UI element a GUI grounding model selects, which undermines the stability of computer-use agents.
brgf3Wa1iv.method: Defines preprocessing transition points where dynamic-resolution preprocessing changes the visual token grid or tile layout, measures UI-element switching around them with controlled interventions, and uses the findings to infer hidden preprocessing settings from clicks and to flag errors from sensitivity to small movements of interface content.
brgf3Wa1iv.key_idea: Dynamic-resolution preprocessing maps raw screenshot sizes to discrete token grids or tile layouts, and the switches at transition points produce unstable clicks.
brgf3Wa1iv.evidence: Eight models and three benchmarks, controlled interventions, and further analysis in two models.
brgf3Wa1iv.claimed_gains: not stated as gains; the abstract reports that the average UI-element switching rate nearly doubles at transition points relative to adjacent one-pixel changes.

w7XgVxBf1Y.one_liner: Replaces in-context demos with two task vectors added to input embeddings of frozen multimodal models.
w7XgVxBf1Y.problem: In-context learning re-encodes demos at every query, and demo-free task-state methods add parameters at per-task-searched locations or at every decoder layer, while inserted tokens or keys cannot change how the original prompt divides attention within a layer.
w7XgVxBf1Y.method: STAVE adds a readout vector to answer-producing token embeddings and a context vector to the other structural token groups, both trained with answer labels on prompts with and without demos. Design choices are justified with a first-order analysis of the loss and a margin bound.
w7XgVxBf1Y.key_idea: Add one readout vector to answer-producing tokens and one context vector to the other structural token groups at the input embeddings, instead of inserting tokens or per-layer states.
w7XgVxBf1Y.evidence: Experiments on six LMMs and five large language models covering multimodal tasks and 18 text tasks, plus a first-order loss analysis and a margin bound.
w7XgVxBf1Y.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms the compared methods on multimodal tasks with far fewer task parameters and surpasses 15-shot ICL and prior task vectors on 18 text tasks, at zero-shot inference cost.

TECUs76Brt.one_liner: Benchmark for instruction following in any-to-any models across text, image and audio context, instruction and output modalities.
TECUs76Brt.problem: Any-to-any models must follow instructions and respond across modalities, including instructions conveyed through images or speech, and this capability needs broad assessment beyond content or format constraints.
TECUs76Brt.method: Introduces Omni-Instruct, with varied context, instruction and output modalities across text, image and audio, and an evaluation framework that decouples output-modality routing from instruction compliance.
TECUs76Brt.key_idea: Separate output-modality routing failures from instruction compliance failures when scoring any-to-any models.
TECUs76Brt.evidence: Evaluation of recent any-to-any models on the benchmark; the abstract does not name models or give counts.
TECUs76Brt.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are that routing failure dominates apparent drops and that models struggle with instructions conveyed through images or speech.

CkuA2Se9vX.one_liner: Evolves prompts against per-subgroup accuracy Pareto objectives using an induced reasoning taxonomy and semantic differential evolution.
CkuA2Se9vX.problem: Prompt optimization guided by scalar validation scores hides performance imbalances across reasoning patterns and yields prompts with competitive overall accuracy but low worst-group accuracy.
CkuA2Se9vX.method: Induces a task-specific taxonomy of mutually exclusive reasoning subgroups from development questions without answer labels and treats subgroup accuracies as Pareto objectives. Semantic differential evolution contrasts Pareto-front and non-front prompts to extract directional semantic patches for mutation and crossover, and meta-rules are induced from trial acceptance outcomes.
CkuA2Se9vX.key_idea: Treat accuracy on label-free induced reasoning subgroups as separate Pareto objectives and mutate prompts using semantic patches that contrast front and non-front prompts.
CkuA2Se9vX.evidence: Experiments across diverse benchmarks (not named in the abstract) and analyses of the induced taxonomy's stability, interpretability and relevance.
CkuA2Se9vX.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports improved worst-group accuracy and reduced disparities across reasoning subgroups without numbers.

dPgomDHPXt.one_liner: Builds simulation-ready articulated assets from one RGB image by retrieving and fitting library assets instead of generating them.
dPgomDHPXt.problem: Generative methods that predict parts and joints for each image mostly fail to settle or move in simulation, and general-purpose agents need a long session of model calls per photograph.
dPgomDHPXt.method: From an RGB image and a task instruction, it locates the object and the part to operate without any box or mask, selects a matching entry from a library of articulated assets, and fits it to the image while keeping its parts and joints intact.
dPgomDHPXt.key_idea: Retrieve a pre-built articulated asset and adapt it to the image while preserving its parts and joints, instead of reconstructing structure from scratch.
dPgomDHPXt.evidence: 2,000 photographs from 31 categories, 50 cluttered images, library growth from 141 to 11,372 entries, five generative baselines, and manipulation tasks built from the assets (abstract truncated).
dPgomDHPXt.claimed_gains: A physically valid asset for 1,713 of 2,000 photographs, task-ready for 53.5% of those labeled, while five generative methods pass on at most 47% and need 6 to 97 times the median GPU time; 162 of 237 annotated objects pass on 50 cluttered images; growing the library from 141 to 11,372 entries raises category coverage from 46% to 100% and top-1 label agreement from 18% to 51%.

Y0CBN3otSQ.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation trains editing models on their own outputs with a clean-conditioned teacher for multi-turn editing.
Y0CBN3otSQ.problem: Editing models degrade rapidly under recursive editing because they are trained on clean source images but must condition on their own imperfect outputs at inference.
Y0CBN3otSQ.method: MT-OPSD trains the model on self-generated conditioning states with editing supervision from a clean-conditioned teacher, without multi-turn annotations. The authors also introduce LME-Bench, 100 ten-turn editing sessions.
Y0CBN3otSQ.key_idea: Distill from a teacher conditioned on clean images into a student conditioned on its own earlier edits, closing the train-test conditioning mismatch.
Y0CBN3otSQ.evidence: Experiments across three editing backbones on LME-Bench (100 ten-turn sessions), with single-turn quality also checked.
Y0CBN3otSQ.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers; the abstract reports substantially improved long-horizon editing success and reduced multi-turn collapse while largely preserving single-turn quality.

7KG7PAwqGD.one_liner: Compresses persistent KV caches with orthogonal alignment across heads or layers, predictive coding and error-bounded quantization.
7KG7PAwqGD.problem: Long-running agents retain KV caches across turns and sessions for hours or days, and compressing these persistent caches must cut storage while controlling reconstruction error.
7KG7PAwqGD.method: Local orthogonal transforms align related heads or layers into a common coordinate frame so token-wise prediction can be combined with same-token prediction across heads or layers. Residuals are quantized on an error-bounded lattice and entropy-coded, with no learned predictors, encoder-side mode search or large joint transforms.
7KG7PAwqGD.key_idea: Align heads or layers with local orthogonal transforms, predict across tokens and across heads or layers, then entropy-code residuals quantized on an error-bounded lattice.
7KG7PAwqGD.evidence: Three attention mechanisms, CPU codec baselines, LongBench-Pro at 128K context, and an SGLang HiCache integration.
7KG7PAwqGD.claimed_gains: Decodes at least 1.6x faster than the evaluated CPU codecs, reaches near-native LongBench-Pro scores at 128K context, and reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42-72% relative to native HiCache with comparable latency.

xVI2HEBl7w.one_liner: Panoramic active mapping that predicts coverage gain with an occupancy prior and a learned beam-search scheduler for aerial exploration.
xVI2HEBl7w.problem: Perspective observations couple viewpoint utility to camera pose, which raises search cost, and large-scale exploration still requires anticipating occluded geometry and allocating computation across candidate trajectories.
xVI2HEBl7w.method: PIONEER combines panoramic evidence with a pretrained occupancy prior to estimate cumulative coverage gain over future observation positions, and a learned scheduler adapts beam-search width and depth using predicted runtime and a planning budget. The authors also build a metric-calibrated UE5-compatible dataset with paired perspective and panoramic observations.
xVI2HEBl7w.key_idea: Estimate cumulative coverage gain at future positions from panoramic observations plus an occupancy prior, and let a learned scheduler set beam-search width and depth under a time budget.
xVI2HEBl7w.evidence: Closed-loop evaluation on a constructed dataset of textured UE5 environments built from 3D assets derived from real-world scenes, at matched exploration time budgets.
xVI2HEBl7w.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers; the abstract reports better coverage and reconstruction quality under matched time budgets and less time to reach a common coverage target (abstract truncated).

NVwYWdQv9b.one_liner: Contrastive distillation that rewards a student by the gap between a strong teacher and a negatively steered copy of itself.
NVwYWdQv9b.problem: Prior contrastive distillation contrasts a task-specific, RL-trained teacher with a base policy, which limits scalability to larger teacher models and broader task domains.
NVwYWdQv9b.method: The student reward is the log-probability gap between a strong teacher and a negatively steered version of the same teacher, steered by a natural-language description of undesirable behavior such as incorrect or non-rigorous reasoning. Analysis uses the Steering-Success Rate.
NVwYWdQv9b.key_idea: Define the contrastive reward as the log-probability gap between the teacher and a prompt-steered worse version of itself, removing task-specific teacher RL.
NVwYWdQv9b.evidence: Mathematical reasoning experiments and ablations, plus a theoretical result relating the Steering-Success Rate to the converged student's win rate over its KL-regularized reference policy under certain conditions.
NVwYWdQv9b.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says negative steering substantially improves the contrastive reward while positive steering gives only marginal gains, and is truncated before results.

YEXEpbOENl.one_liner: Video generation system combining trainable NVFP4 sparse quantized attention, NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation.
YEXEpbOENl.problem: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, and jointly adapting to sparsity, low-bit quantization and few-step denoising is difficult, especially under aggressive NVFP4 quantization.
YEXEpbOENl.method: Trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA) with custom inference kernels that fuse native NVFP4 computation, combined with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation through a staged training recipe.
YEXEpbOENl.key_idea: Fuse sparse attention and native NVFP4 computation in custom kernels, and adapt the model to quantization, sparsity and few-step denoising in stages.
YEXEpbOENl.evidence: Kernel timings against FlashAttention on different hardware and end-to-end results on Wan2.1-14B on an RTX 5090.
YEXEpbOENl.claimed_gains: At 90% sparsity VSQA accelerates attention 8-29x over FlashAttention, and on Wan2.1-14B the model reaches 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 with comparable video quality.

lcKH15FSIp.one_liner: Turns a static 3D Gaussian Splatting scene into a seamlessly looping 4D cinemagraph using a periodic deformation field.
lcKH15FSIp.problem: Existing 3D world models produce frozen scenes, and prior Eulerian cinemagraph methods are limited to fluid-like motion.
lcKH15FSIp.method: A vision-language model infers plausible dynamics and guides a video model to synthesize a reference video, which is lifted and completed into multi-view videos. Inconsistency-Robust Periodic 4DGS then fits a Fourier-series deformation field that loops by construction, plus a Grounded Drift Field anchored at the reference view to absorb cross-view inconsistency.
lcKH15FSIp.key_idea: Parameterize deformation with a Fourier series so loops are exact by construction, and absorb multi-view inconsistency in a separate drift field anchored at the reference view.
lcKH15FSIp.evidence: 39 reconstructed and generated scenes, a ground-truth-free evaluation covering vividness, naturalness, loop seam coherence and scene quality, and user studies.
lcKH15FSIp.claimed_gains: Outperforms all baselines on 39 scenes and wins 70.8%-99.0% of user-study comparisons.

GuKWmNBY5l.one_liner: Generates artist-style meshes by flow-based parallel triangle prediction on an octree-aligned bounding volume hierarchy, then half-edge stitching.
GuKWmNBY5l.problem: Flow-based methods that generate vertices first and recover faces from predicted connectivity let edge errors propagate into invalid surfaces.
GuKWmNBY5l.method: Triangles are organized in an octree-aligned bounding volume hierarchy (OctBVH) whose nested boxes give local frames for coarse-to-fine prediction and allow sparse convolutions. A hierarchical VAE and conditional flow priors generate triangle soups from point clouds or images, and EdgeMatch recovers connectivity through learned half-edge matching with explicit checks against non-manifold edges, duplicate faces and collapsed triangles.
GuKWmNBY5l.key_idea: Predict triangles first, in parallel, on a nested-box hierarchy and stitch them with learned half-edge matching plus explicit topology validity checks.
