wODuGIZFpv.problem: Temporal-centric KV memories in streaming video diffusion cause identity drift and semantic inconsistency when entities exit frames or prompts change.
wODuGIZFpv.method: SlotMemory decomposes the transformer's KV manifold into discrete semantic slots that serve as routing addresses to retrieve stored original KV tokens by entity identity and prompt relevance.
wODuGIZFpv.key_idea: Uses discrete semantic slots as routing addresses over stored transformer KV tokens for object-centric retrieval during streaming diffusion.
wODuGIZFpv.evidence: Evaluations on 30-second and 60-second interactive narratives using the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone against memory-based streaming baselines.
wODuGIZFpv.claimed_gains: At the 30-second horizon, SlotMemory improves Dynamic Degree by 31.2% over MemFlow and leads in Total and Quality scores.

0a8ebRImO1.one_liner: Mitigates financial agent hallucinations via task-adaptive execution, candidate evidence verification, and verified skill accumulation.
0a8ebRImO1.problem: LLM financial agents suffer from hallucinations caused by evidence misalignment, context noise accumulation, and unreliable experience reuse.
0a8ebRImO1.method: FinHarness combines task-adaptive execution, candidate evidence verification to ground reasoning, and verified skill accumulation for cross-task reuse.
0a8ebRImO1.key_idea: Integrates candidate evidence verification with verified skill accumulation into a task-adaptive financial agent workflow.
0a8ebRImO1.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM backbones on a professional financial reasoning benchmark and an out-of-domain stock-trading task.
0a8ebRImO1.claimed_gains: Achieves gains of up to 19.89% over baselines, reduces hallucination rate among erroneous responses by up to 73.23%, and raises reasoning score from 41.86% to 52.08% with accumulated skills.

pCoycIKknm.one_liner: Feeds the previous top-layer hidden state back into the input via a gated linear unit at each decoding step.
pCoycIKknm.problem: Standard autoregressive transformers discard top-layer hidden states between tokens, leaving a narrow vertical feedback channel.
pCoycIKknm.method: The full-bandwidth transformer fuses the previous step's top-layer hidden state with the sampled token embedding using a gated linear unit and feeds it back as the next input. It is trained with a scheduled multi-pass objective that introduces latent feedback late in pretraining and mixes deeper feedback passes.
pCoycIKknm.key_idea: Fuses the prior token's top-layer hidden state with the next token embedding via a gated linear unit, trained with a scheduled multi-pass objective.
pCoycIKknm.evidence: Evaluated by pretraining 1B-parameter models up to 400B tokens on validation loss, 5-shot LM tasks, math/coding generation, and instruction tuning.

zbjwSwvqId.one_liner: Controls and transfers demonstrated camera viewpoint changes alongside visual edits in image analogy.
zbjwSwvqId.problem: Image-analogy editing becomes ambiguous when the exemplar pair includes a camera viewpoint change in addition to a visual edit.
zbjwSwvqId.method: PanToMime enables camera-aware image analogy to transfer, match, or suppress demonstrated camera changes alongside visual edits. The authors also build PanToMime-Bench and Render2Real, a geometry-grounded pipeline for generating multi-view training pairs.
zbjwSwvqId.key_idea: Disentangles and controls camera viewpoint transformations during exemplar-based image analogy, supported by geometry-grounded multi-view synthetic data (Render2Real).
zbjwSwvqId.evidence: Evaluated on PanToMime-Bench against existing image-analogy baselines using camera orientation error and Edit score.
zbjwSwvqId.claimed_gains: Reduces camera orientation error from 68.20 degrees (second-best) to 30.69 degrees while retaining an Edit score of 9.03.

Q9AHmuAk4Y.one_liner: Benchmarks whether frozen-weight AI agents can recursively improve their own Pi harnesses across held-out tasks.
Q9AHmuAk4Y.problem: It is unclear whether current AI agents can recursively improve their own harnesses and whether such harness gains generalize to unseen tasks.
Q9AHmuAk4Y.method: RSIBench iteratively lets an agent use task trajectories to revise its open-source Pi harness while keeping model weights fixed, committing revisions that improve training scores. Final harnesses are evaluated on held-out tasks across 100 tasks in Terminal, Environment Learning, SWE, and Science.
Q9AHmuAk4Y.key_idea: Evaluates iterative trajectory-driven revisions of an open-source agent harness under frozen model weights on held-out tasks using RSI lift.
Q9AHmuAk4Y.evidence: Seven models are evaluated on 100 tasks across Terminal, Environment Learning, SWE, and Science.
Q9AHmuAk4Y.claimed_gains: Claude Opus 5 achieves an RSI lift of +8.3 percentage points (36.4 to 44.7) across held-out tasks, while GPT-5.5 loses 8.3 points on held-out Science tasks (11.1 to 2.8).

IRHuEpKDcZ.one_liner: Replay-tested harness edits let a fixed vision-language model improve observation and action during continuous game play.
IRHuEpKDcZ.problem: Existing game agents often depend on game-state APIs, inference pauses, or repeated attempts rather than learning during continuous graphical-interface play.
IRHuEpKDcZ.method: GamePilot places a fixed-weight vision-language model inside editable harness code controlling observations and actions. Its Evolver localizes failures, admits revisions through offline replay tests, and chooses the next harness version by estimated advantage in the inherited state.
IRHuEpKDcZ.key_idea: Revise executable observation-and-action harness code through failure localization, offline replay validation, and inherited-state version selection.
IRHuEpKDcZ.evidence: GamePilot Bench evaluates four games through one-hour Milestone campaigns plus Atomic and Basic tasks, with Gemini 3.6 Flash used for the reported Milestone comparison.
IRHuEpKDcZ.claimed_gains: With Gemini 3.6 Flash, GamePilot reaches 1.85–2.00× the Milestone progress of the strongest baseline in every game, while observation and action revisions together with game knowledge add 10.6–11.4 percentage points.

IrtiY8LY4F.one_liner: Attack-and-repair task synthesis turns research papers and artifacts into executable, human-reviewed computer science research environments.
IrtiY8LY4F.problem: Converting research papers and released artifacts into executable agent tasks is difficult because objectives, constraints, and evaluation protocols must become explicit.
IrtiY8LY4F.method: CSForge filters papers, synthesizes structured tasks, and deploys environments from published artifacts. Iterative attack-and-repair removes shortcut solutions, while reproduced reference experiments and repeated runs check consistency with source artifacts and reported findings.
IrtiY8LY4F.key_idea: Iteratively attack task evaluation protocols and repair shortcuts before deploying artifact-checked executable research environments.
IrtiY8LY4F.evidence: Construction experiments sample filter-passing papers from seven computer science subfields, assess executable environments through human quality review, and test six frontier models.
IrtiY8LY4F.claimed_gains: Across sampled filter-passing papers from seven CS subfields, 86.8% of construction attempts yield executable environments and 80.0% yield environments that pass human quality review.

x6HbrJXR6m.one_liner: Spectral and divergence-based mutual information metrics assess and optimize dynamic graph embeddings without downstream labels.
x6HbrJXR6m.problem: Downstream-task evaluation of dynamic graph embeddings offers little direct diagnostic insight and causes repeated tuning and unstable model selection.
x6HbrJXR6m.method: IDG defines structure mutual information using spectral entropy and feature mutual information using f-divergence. It also incorporates both metrics into a representation-learning objective for embedding optimization.
x6HbrJXR6m.key_idea: Measure structural information and node-attribute dependence in latent embeddings, then optimize those information-theoretic quantities directly.
x6HbrJXR6m.evidence: Experiments examine positive empirical associations between the proposed metrics and downstream performance, but the supplied abstract truncates the datasets and numerical results.

p4ZXFYp9jK.one_liner: Composing depth-specific individual adaptations creates distinguishable LLM agents with more varied collective behavior.
p4ZXFYp9jK.problem: Prompting many agents from one shared model compresses human variation into a small set of similar simulated voices.
p4ZXFYp9jK.method: ReMap learns individual variation from real writing through lightweight weight adaptation, then composes adaptations across model depth to assemble agents from multiple source individuals.
p4ZXFYp9jK.key_idea: Compose individually learned weight adaptations at different model depths to synthesize new population members.
p4ZXFYp9jK.evidence: Experiments span three domains and six backbones, comparing human-writing similarity, mutual distinguishability, and collective behavior with prompted populations in external simulators.

KvnInP7Vy6.one_liner: Motion-derived localization targets supervise visual representations to ground robot actions under camera-extrinsic changes.
KvnInP7Vy6.problem: Camera perturbations can induce directional trajectory drift in VLA policies that exploit pixel-coordinate shortcuts instead of robot-object geometry.
KvnInP7Vy6.method: S³-VLA adds a self-supervised auxiliary grounding objective that recovers motion-derived robot localization targets from visual representations. The objective implicitly guides policy attention toward the robot without requiring external spatial labels.
KvnInP7Vy6.key_idea: Use robot motion to generate localization targets that supervise visual self-grounding within the VLA policy.
KvnInP7Vy6.evidence: Simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks evaluate two VLA backbones, π0.5 and GR00T-N1.6, including camera-extrinsic perturbations.
KvnInP7Vy6.claimed_gains: Under camera-extrinsic perturbations, S³-VLA increases the average success rate on real-world tasks from 16.4% to 29.4%.

dcQKvnC6cP.one_liner: Deep recurrent trajectories self-distill their shared block through one pass, improving later shallow and deep execution.
dcQKvnC6cP.problem: Additional recurrent execution exposes improved predictions that ordinary inference does not write back into the shared recurrent computation.
dcQKvnC6cP.method: Preference write-back self-distills trajectories from deeper execution into only the shared recurrent block without another correctness signal. Training updates the block through one recurrent pass rather than the full target depth.
dcQKvnC6cP.key_idea: Self-distill deep recurrent trajectories through a single shared-block pass so later executions internalize depth-induced preferences.
dcQKvnC6cP.evidence: A 1B model retrofitted with recurrent depth is evaluated on GSM8K at mean depths 4, 8, and 32, with controlled comparisons of looping recipes and training depths.
dcQKvnC6cP.claimed_gains: On a 1B model at mean depth 4, GSM8K accuracy at the model's own depth rises from 56.2% to 62.7%, with comparable gains at mean depths 8 and 32.

znMifjkjwr.one_liner: Densifies RLVR rewards with policy-derived trajectory informativeness and a token-level hinge penalizing overconfident wrong decisions.
znMifjkjwr.problem: Binary outcome rewards in GRPO-based RLVR cause Zero-Advantage Collapse on uniform-outcome groups and Hallucinated Certainty on wrong rollouts late in training.
znMifjkjwr.method: ISPO (Intrinsic Signal Policy Optimization) augments binary outcome supervision with intrinsic signals computed solely from the policy's own conditional probabilities. It combines a sequence-level signal scoring how informative the reasoning trace is for the final answer with a token-level directional hinge penalty on confidently wrong decision tokens.
znMifjkjwr.key_idea: Combines sequence-level reasoning-to-answer informativeness with a token-level hinge penalty on overconfident wrong tokens from policy probabilities.
znMifjkjwr.evidence: Evaluated across three base models and five mathematical reasoning benchmarks alongside training-dynamics diagnostics.

geNcJUXYtu.one_liner: Uses interval arithmetic to bound worst-case layer response changes over continuous activation regions during machine unlearning.
geNcJUXYtu.problem: Intensive unlearning updates degrade retained knowledge because existing preservation losses protect retained behavior only indirectly or at finitely many points.
geNcJUXYtu.method: BARRIER identifies an activation-space control region for targeted erasure and uses interval arithmetic to derive a closed-form bound on the worst-case change of protected layers over continuous regions of activation space. This architecture-agnostic bound serves as a preservation objective compatible with existing erasure losses.
geNcJUXYtu.key_idea: Constrains unlearning updates using closed-form interval-arithmetic bounds on worst-case layer output changes over continuous activation regions.
geNcJUXYtu.evidence: Theoretical per-layer guarantee analysis and empirical evaluations across classification and generative settings.

XZyV1E5COA.one_liner: Replaces error feedback in biased distributed gradient compression with coordinatewise sign-memory acute-angle constraints.
XZyV1E5COA.problem: Error feedback for biased gradient compression in distributed optimization requires storing at least one extra full-precision model-sized vector per node.
XZyV1E5COA.method: The authors propose ACTION, which enforces a non-negative inner product between the global gradient and aggregated compression error, and its practical variant L-ACTION, which enforces coordinatewise alignment against the previous aggregated compressed gradient. L-ACTION stores only the signs of the reference gradient as auxiliary memory.
XZyV1E5COA.key_idea: Enforces coordinatewise acute-angle alignment with the lagged aggregated compressed gradient using only sign-level auxiliary state.
XZyV1E5COA.evidence: Theoretical convergence guarantees for ACTION under non-contractive generalized biased compressors and a residual-term convergence bound for L-ACTION.

QZN7WgUfvg.one_liner: Allocates tree-search supervision budgets to high-utility agent decisions selected by branch-outcome dispersion.
QZN7WgUfvg.problem: Dense process supervision for long-horizon language agents treats credit assignment purely as reward density, ignoring that identical credit budgets have heterogeneous marginal utility across decisions.
QZN7WgUfvg.method: The authors define Credit Assignment Geometry along Quantity, Heterogeneity, and Utility, showing diminishing returns from quantity alone and large variance from allocation choice. Based on this, Mem-C measures branch-outcome dispersion to identify high-utility decision steps and focus branching credit allocation there.
QZN7WgUfvg.key_idea: Uses branch-outcome dispersion to identify high-utility steps and allocate a fixed tree-supervision budget preferentially to those decisions.
QZN7WgUfvg.evidence: Evaluated under matched credit budgets against baselines across three transfer benchmarks.

uZBAW51QWn.one_liner: Trains LLMs to formulate and revise constraint programs via two-stage SFT and solver-event-grouped GRPO.
uZBAW51QWn.problem: LLM constraint-programming systems generate code once or use fixed repair rules, missing semantic modeling errors such as omitted constraints, wrong domains, or incorrect objectives.
uZBAW51QWn.method: CPARL combines two-stage CP-specific SFT (general modeling/revision demonstrations followed by error-targeted demonstrations) with agentic RL that controls direct generation, solver-assisted edits, solver calls, and termination. Its Solver-Event GRPO (SE-GRPO) groups decisions between successive solver evaluations and assigns credit from incremental solver evidence anchored by semantic validation; the authors also introduce the NL4CP benchmark.
uZBAW51QWn.key_idea: Groups agent decisions between consecutive solver calls in SE-GRPO and assigns credit using incremental solver feedback anchored by semantic validation.
uZBAW51QWn.evidence: Evaluated on the newly constructed NL4CP benchmark of formally specified problems and additional benchmarks.

gz1uCUDsqV.one_liner: Benchmarks hyperbolic Transformer representations, operators, and module compatibility across 556 controlled experimental runs.
gz1uCUDsqV.problem: Hyperbolic Transformer papers change geometric manifolds, operators, and training settings simultaneously, obscuring whether gains come from the hyperbolic representation or specific operators.
gz1uCUDsqV.method: HypTBench provides a unified benchmark for Hyperbolic Transformers that systematically evaluates Lorentz and Poincaré manifold methods alongside individual Transformer operators and cross-module compatibility.
gz1uCUDsqV.key_idea: Decouples hyperbolic manifold choice, Transformer operators, and module compatibility in a unified benchmark across controlled runs.
gz1uCUDsqV.evidence: 556 experimental runs comparing Lorentz and Poincaré manifold methods and module combinations across tasks.

LOCGHgwYcN.one_liner: Retrieves camera-frustum-overlapping memory and retains pre-edit observations as structural depth in a camera-conditioned video DiT.
LOCGHgwYcN.problem: Unifying camera navigation and semantic editing in video world models causes context forgetting on revisits and makes pre-edit RGB observations visually obsolete yet geometrically valuable.
LOCGHgwYcN.method: MemWorld augments a camera-conditioned video DiT with a validity-aware multimodal memory that retrieves nonlocal frames via camera-frustum overlap. A version-conditioned RGB-depth policy keeps current appearance in RGB while converting obsolete pre-edit observations into structural depth, processed jointly with recent history and current latents.
LOCGHgwYcN.key_idea: Retrieves nonlocal history by camera-frustum overlap and applies a version-conditioned policy keeping current views as RGB and pre-edit views as structural depth.
LOCGHgwYcN.evidence: Evaluated on a proposed 500-case editing/navigation/revisitation benchmark, R2M-Bench, and MBench.

Z9T4V5Tjo8.one_liner: Replaces Monte Carlo ELBO gradient sampling in neural set-function variational inference with a learned continuous relaxation surrogate.
Z9T4V5Tjo8.problem: Optimal subset oracle training of neural set functions uses Monte Carlo ELBO gradient estimation in mean-field variational inference, causing high compute cost and noisy optimization.
Z9T4V5Tjo8.method: The authors reinterpret the ELBO as a continuous relaxation of the set function and learn a surrogate objective to provide deterministic continuous gradients during variational updates. They also derive an approximation guarantee under submodular maximization and connect the objective to variational free energy.
Z9T4V5Tjo8.key_idea: Learns a continuous surrogate objective for the ELBO relaxation of neural set functions to eliminate Monte Carlo gradient sampling during mean-field variational updates.
Z9T4V5Tjo8.evidence: Theoretical approximation guarantee for submodular maximization plus experiments on real-world subset selection tasks against existing baselines.

OwbT4EloeN.one_liner: Extracts an ownership-bias activation direction from paired attribution prompts and projects it out during LLM verification inference.
OwbT4EloeN.problem: LLMs acting as verifiers rate identical artifacts more favorably when attributed to themselves, introducing ownership bias that degrades impartial verification.
OwbT4EloeN.method: The framework holds the evaluated artifact fixed while varying claimed authorship to isolate ownership bias, extracts a dominant ownership-associated direction from paired internal activations, and projects that direction out at inference time while monitoring correctness-related controls.
OwbT4EloeN.key_idea: Identifies an authorship-attribution direction from paired internal activations on fixed artifacts and removes it via inference-time projection.
OwbT4EloeN.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLMs, tasks, new benchmarks, and varied attribution phrasings against correctness controls.

jfq0Rcq97f.one_liner: Jointly predicts multi-agent participation, roles, and directed edges in parallel using directional role-context encodings and RL.
jfq0Rcq97f.problem: Multi-agent LLM collaboration methods fix team size, select from preset topologies, or build graphs sequentially, and fail to distinguish incoming versus outgoing local role relationships.
jfq0Rcq97f.method: RCGP formulates agent participation, functional roles, and directed communication in a unified query-conditioned graph-policy action space that makes parallel node-edge decisions. It introduces directional role-context encodings separating receiving and sending neighborhood diversity and support, optimized via execution-guided reinforcement learning.
jfq0Rcq97f.key_idea: Makes parallel node-and-edge graph policy decisions conditioned on separate receiving and sending directional role-context encodings trained with execution-guided RL.
jfq0Rcq97f.evidence: Evaluated with execution-guided reinforcement learning on multi-agent LLM collaboration tasks.

itVce8sgQ4.one_liner: Reverses importance-sampling ratio weighting on positive-advantage tokens in outcome-supervised LLM RL to prevent entropy collapse.
itVce8sgQ4.problem: In outcome-supervised RL like GRPO, importance sampling ratios double as token-level credit weights, upweighting already-rising positive tokens and causing entropy collapse and repetition.
itVce8sgQ4.method: Asymmetric Importance Sampling Policy Optimization (ASPO) reverses the ratio-induced weighting for positive-advantage tokens while stabilizing extreme updates and preserving gradient flow for unmasked tokens.
itVce8sgQ4.key_idea: Inverts importance-sampling ratio weighting on positive-advantage tokens to eliminate rich-get-richer token amplification in outcome-supervised RL.
itVce8sgQ4.evidence: Analyzed and evaluated in outcome-supervised RL post-training of LLMs.

TEPGe6SHQR.one_liner: Trains one dexterous manipulation policy across parallel dense motion-tracking and noised sparse-reward generalization environments.
TEPGe6SHQR.problem: Goal-reaching RL for multi-finger hands produces unnatural strategies without human priors, while motion tracking reproduces single reference clips but cannot generalize off-reference.
TEPGe6SHQR.method: AdaDex uses Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking to train a shared goal-conditioned policy from a few seconds of human mocap or RGB(D)-reconstructed hand-object motion across two massively parallel environment populations: motion-tracking environments with dense tracking rewards and generalization environments with noised initial states/goals and sparse object-success rewards.
TEPGe6SHQR.key_idea: Co-trains one goal-conditioned policy on parallel dense motion-tracking environments for human priors and perturbed sparse-reward environments for off-reference generalization.
TEPGe6SHQR.evidence: Evaluated against baselines on functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and throw-and-catch skills.

QcKNgMEDvQ.one_liner: Accelerates few-step video diffusion by reconstructing skipped-frame transformer block residuals via linear interpolation between nearest anchor frames.
QcKNgMEDvQ.problem: Each step of 4-step distilled video diffusion remains expensive, and existing frame-sparse inference loses accuracy by reconstructing full block outputs or over-smoothing via all-anchor averaging.
QcKNgMEDvQ.method: BlockDelta is a training-free frame-sparse inference method that computes only anchor frames inside each transformer block and reconstructs skipped frames' block residuals (output minus input) instead of full outputs. It estimates skipped residuals via linear interpolation between the two nearest enclosing anchors rather than averaging all anchors.
QcKNgMEDvQ.key_idea: Reconstructs skipped frames' transformer block residuals rather than full outputs by linearly interpolating between the two nearest enclosing anchor frames.
QcKNgMEDvQ.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation on few-step video diffusion models.

i50FJ0LqXO.one_liner: Augments Distribution Matching Distillation with population-level Sinkhorn-divergence matching between intermediate student and teacher rollouts.
i50FJ0LqXO.problem: Distribution Matching Distillation relies on mode-seeking reverse KL that collapses sample diversity, while paired trajectory regularizers restrictively enforce fixed noise-to-sample correspondences.
i50FJ0LqXO.method: Energy-Guided Distribution Matching Distillation (EG-DMD) rolls out multiple student and teacher trajectories to an intermediate diffusion time at each training step and aligns their empirical distributions with a Sinkhorn-divergence energy loss alongside DMD, optimizing population coupling without pairing individual noise vectors.
i50FJ0LqXO.key_idea: Matches multi-trajectory student and teacher intermediate empirical distributions via Sinkhorn divergence to preserve teacher modes without paired trajectory regression.
i50FJ0LqXO.evidence: Evaluated across diffusion models with diverse architectures against DMD and diversity-preserving distillation baselines.

IyAZeT4abc.one_liner: Couples gradient-complete feature manifold constraints with non-parametric kernel shift compensation for exemplar-free class-incremental learning.
IyAZeT4abc.problem: Exemplar-free class-incremental learning methods treat backbone feature drift and post-hoc prototype misalignment separately, ignoring their geometric coupling through the classifier's pullback metric.
IyAZeT4abc.method: CAMP formulates manifold preservation and classifier recalibration as a coupled geometric pipeline. It combines Feature Manifold Constraint (FMC) for gradient-complete manifold regularization during training with Kernel Shift Compensation (KSC), a non-parametric minimax-optimal estimator correcting residual drift.
IyAZeT4abc.key_idea: Interlocks a gradient-complete feature manifold constraint during training with a non-parametric minimax-optimal kernel shift estimator to jointly preserve manifold geometry and recalibrate class prototypes.
IyAZeT4abc.evidence: Provides a geometric pullback-metric formulation and exemplar-free class-incremental learning experiments (specific datasets not named in the abstract excerpt).

kQkih2eMHu.one_liner: Conditions single-pass image restoration on predicted failure locations and region-specific corrective guidance to fix local artifacts.
kQkih2eMHu.problem: Image restoration models achieve high global fidelity but still leave localized perceptual failures on semantically sensitive regions such as faces and text.
kQkih2eMHu.method: Failure-Aware Image Restoration (FAIR) replaces uniform whole-image generative priors with region-bound conditioning in a single-pass restoration model, specifying both where local failures are likely to occur and what corrective guidance each region needs.
kQkih2eMHu.key_idea: Conditions a single-pass restoration model on spatial maps of likely local failure regions paired with region-specific corrective guidance rather than applying a uniform global prior.
kQkih2eMHu.evidence: Supported by experiments evaluating local failure resolution and perceptual quality across restoration pipelines (specific datasets not named in the abstract).

6LPQVnHdF5.one_liner: Optimizes diffusion-drafted speculative decoding throughput via prefix-acceptance loss factorization and latency-aware configuration search.
6LPQVnHdF5.problem: Higher proposal capacity or mean accepted tokens in diffusion drafters often fails to raise speculative decoding throughput due to early prefix rejections and higher per-round latency.
6LPQVnHdF5.method: DScout factorizes drafter training loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction components—combining mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss to align supervision with prefix acceptance. At inference, it factorizes throughput as MAT over per-round latency to search target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and block size per workload.
6LPQVnHdF5.key_idea: Factorizes drafter training into prefix-acceptance-aligned objectives and inference throughput into MAT-to-latency ratios to select high-throughput conditioning depth, drafter depth, and block size.
6LPQVnHdF5.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B against autoregressive decoding and prior speculative decoding baselines.
6LPQVnHdF5.claimed_gains: Achieves 3.70x and 3.97x mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, improving mean speedup over the strongest baseline by 8.3% and 5.8%.

5X0hQbcpwk.one_liner: Reconciles per-step candidate optimizer updates by plasticity benefit and stability cost to curb MLLM forgetting.
5X0hQbcpwk.problem: Fine-tuning multimodal large language models on specialized tasks degrades pre-trained general capabilities, and parameter-level regulation ignores how individual optimizer updates shape forgetting.
5X0hQbcpwk.method: SPUR (Selective Per-step Update Reconciliation) treats each candidate optimizer update coordinate as a decision object at every step. It estimates plasticity benefit from target loss reduction and stability cost from predicted deviation from pre-trained behavior, then applies only the globally highest-utility coordinates.
5X0hQbcpwk.key_idea: Recomputes a utility score trading off target-loss reduction against predicted deviation from pre-trained behavior to select update coordinates at every optimization step.

7CNpxGctIe.one_liner: Scales sequential recommenders via cross-depth aggregation, sparse latent experts, and structure-aware optimization.
7CNpxGctIe.problem: Increasing model size in sequential recommendation often fails to yield proportional performance gains while making optimization harder.
7CNpxGctIe.method: TriScaleRec combines adaptive cross-depth representation aggregation with sparse latent-space expert computation that controls active compute. It pairs this architecture with structure-aware optimization (Muon) to sustain training at larger model scales.
7CNpxGctIe.key_idea: Aggregates representations across depths, expands capacity with sparse latent-space experts, and trains with structure-aware optimization to maintain scaling gains.
7CNpxGctIe.evidence: Evaluated on multiple public sequential recommendation benchmarks and scaling experiments across six progressively larger model configurations.

ii0KmDkxuS.one_liner: Clusters time-series agent failures to synthesize evidence-only tools filtered by a paired admission gate.
ii0KmDkxuS.problem: Pre-supplied human-curated tools can hurt time-series agent accuracy on some tasks, while generic self-revision introduces silent regressions hidden by average scores.
ii0KmDkxuS.method: TimeEvo clusters an agent's diagnosed failures into capability gaps, plans a measurement for each gap, and synthesizes evidence-only tools to fill them. Candidate tool libraries are admitted only after passing a paired admission gate.
ii0KmDkxuS.key_idea: Synthesizes evidence-only measurement tools for clustered failure modes and accepts candidate libraries only through a paired admission gate.
ii0KmDkxuS.evidence: Evaluated on ten time series QA tasks across three backbones, including cross-backbone transfer from a cheap model to stronger ones.
ii0KmDkxuS.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy on every task and every backbone starting from an empty library (generic self-revision changed 147 answers and broke 56 while moving the score by less than a point; exact TimeEvo margins not stated).

E0DQIlOn5X.one_liner: Uses ridge regression on pretraining scores and mixture composition to predict post-SFT data mixture rankings.
E0DQIlOn5X.problem: Pretraining data mixture selection typically ranks candidates before post-training, assuming pretraining rankings survive mid-training and supervised fine-tuning.
E0DQIlOn5X.method: After studying 106 1.5B-parameter models across pretraining mixtures with identical mid-training and SFT, the authors propose MixSelector. It fits ridge regression on a small subset of post-trained candidates to weight pretraining scores and mixture composition, then ranks remaining candidates.
E0DQIlOn5X.key_idea: Fits ridge regression on a subset of post-trained models to combine pretraining benchmark scores and mixture composition into post-SFT ranking predictions.
E0DQIlOn5X.evidence: Experimental study of 106 1.5B-parameter models differing only in pretraining mixtures with identical mid-training and SFT, evaluated on held-out candidates across knowledge, math, and code.
E0DQIlOn5X.claimed_gains: Achieves a mean Spearman correlation of 0.72 with post-SFT rankings on held-out candidates across capability families, versus 0.10 for a fixed-weight pretraining composite.

8ytqtZr2QM.one_liner: Introduces NavSafe-infinity, a 280-scenario photorealistic closed-loop benchmark for evaluating autonomous driving safety.
8ytqtZr2QM.problem: Open-loop autonomous driving benchmarks cannot measure whether end-to-end policies resist compounding errors, recover from failures, or interact safely with road actors.
8ytqtZr2QM.method: NavSafe-infinity provides 280 photorealistic closed-loop scenarios across 28 event types with structured success and failure criteria. It scores policies across four traffic-safety categories: Traffic Crashes, Vulnerable Road User Crashes, Traffic Violations, and Traffic Incidents.
8ytqtZr2QM.key_idea: Evaluates end-to-end driving policies in 280 closed-loop photorealistic scenarios spanning 28 event types under a four-category traffic-safety taxonomy.
8ytqtZr2QM.evidence: Evaluates 20 end-to-end driving policies and analyzes passive demonstration perturbation and open-loop reinforcement-learning fine-tuning.

PRYmmv10Qt.one_liner: Introduces CPSE-Bench, an execution-grounded repository benchmark for coding agents on cyber-physical systems.
PRYmmv10Qt.problem: Generic unit-tested coding benchmarks do not reveal whether coding agents can engineer cyber-physical systems requiring closed-loop behavioral validation.
PRYmmv10Qt.method: CPSE-Bench collects real engineering issues across thirteen production driving, robotics, and aerial autonomy repositories, pairing each issue with a containerized behavioral reproducer verified against the buggy and maintainer-repaired versions. Tasks are organized into eight literature-grounded cyber-physical capability suites.
PRYmmv10Qt.key_idea: Pairs historical cyber-physical repository issues with containerized behavioral reproducers verified on buggy and fixed versions across eight capability suites.
PRYmmv10Qt.evidence: Evaluates nine models using mini-SWE-agent across thirteen production repositories spanning driving, robotics, and aerial autonomy.
PRYmmv10Qt.claimed_gains: The strongest evaluated model resolves only 73.5% of tasks on CPSE-Bench.

aA7Lek5D7g.one_liner: Uses a hypernetwork to convert verbal supervisor feedback on failed trajectories into test-time low-rank weight updates.
aA7Lek5D7g.problem: Agentic reinforcement learning relies on expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its usefulness for test-time agent adaptation.
aA7Lek5D7g.method: Verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) connects an agent and a supervisor in a closed loop via a hypernetwork. The supervisor produces natural-language feedback from failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork maps that verbal supervision to low-rank weight updates for the agent at test time.
aA7Lek5D7g.key_idea: Maps natural-language feedback from a supervisor on failed trajectories into low-rank agent weight updates through a hypernetwork in a closed loop.
aA7Lek5D7g.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3-4B on ALFWorld (in-distribution split) and WebShop against GRPO and Reflexion.
aA7Lek5D7g.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-4B, vSFT outperforms GRPO and Reflexion by 11.5% and 10.8% in success rate on ALFWorld's in-distribution split, and by 4.8% and 18.2% on WebShop.

YupgzJiSw9.one_liner: Diagnoses MoE routing collapse via unselected-expert router gradients and validates a gradient intervention.
YupgzJiSw9.problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models suffer from routing collapse where tokens concentrate on a few experts, degrading performance and compute efficiency.
YupgzJiSw9.method: The authors run a controlled pretraining study showing that early representation reorganization perturbs routing while sparse router gradients for unselected experts vanish or lose expert-specific signals. They introduce a targeted router gradient intervention that restores expert-specific gradients for unselected experts while keeping forward routing sparse.
YupgzJiSw9.key_idea: Restores expert-specific router gradient signals for unselected experts during backward passes while preserving sparse forward routing without an auxiliary loss.
YupgzJiSw9.evidence: Controlled pretraining study across two model scales and eight model variants, plus validation of the router gradient intervention.

AYLzyXh4ed.one_liner: Queries a frozen time-series foundation model at multiple temporal resolutions and reconciles forecasts via weighted least squares.
AYLzyXh4ed.problem: Standard zero-shot inference queries frozen time-series foundation models only at the original temporal resolution, leaving multi-scale predictive signals unused.
AYLzyXh4ed.method: Adaptive Multi-Resolution Inference (AMRI) aggregates observed history to multiple temporal resolutions and queries the same frozen foundation model on each. Using structural aggregation constraints and forecast reliability calibrated from historical errors before testing, AMRI reconciles the outputs via closed-form weighted least squares without gradient updates.
AYLzyXh4ed.key_idea: Reconciles multi-resolution forecasts from a frozen time-series foundation model via closed-form weighted least squares using historically calibrated error weights.
AYLzyXh4ed.evidence: Provides an expected squared-error guarantee under unbiased errors and exact inverse-covariance weighting; empirical datasets beyond drought prediction keyword are not stated in the abstract.

1cNggKmyeh.one_liner: Decouples long-term agent memory into high-recall retrieval and RL-trained query-conditioned evidence distillation.
1cNggKmyeh.problem: Preconstructing agent memory units before queries are known yields coarse, noisy retrievals that burden downstream answerers on long conversational histories.
1cNggKmyeh.method: DeferMem separates memory access into high-recall candidate retrieval followed by a memory distiller that selects messages and rewrites query-conditioned evidence. The distiller is trained with DistillPO, an RL algorithm using a decomposed-and-gated reward pipeline and structure-aligned advantage assignment.
1cNggKmyeh.key_idea: Trains a post-retrieval memory distiller with RL over message selection and evidence rewriting using gated rewards and structure-aligned advantages.

z49XjWjCqb.one_liner: Synthesizes verified multi-turn agent SFT trajectories from environment specifications without task seeds.
z49XjWjCqb.problem: Building executable agent training trajectories for new environments typically requires manual task design, interaction orchestration, and outcome verification.
z49XjWjCqb.method: SAGE induces requests directly from domain context, tool interfaces, user attributes, and initial states without query seeds or reference solutions. A persistent user generator interacts with an agent while an isolated verifier filters requests pre-execution and trajectories post-execution, converting accepted runs into SFT data.
z49XjWjCqb.key_idea: Generates seedless agent requests from environment specs, runs multi-turn user-agent interactions, and filters requests and trajectories with an isolated verifier for SFT.
z49XjWjCqb.evidence: Data generated with Qwen3.8-2.4T, Qwen3.8-Next-Flash, GLM5.2, and Kimi-K3 teachers; SFT evaluated on Qwen3.5-27B across General Avg, BFCL Multi-turn, Tau2Bench three-domain Overall, and SWE-bench Lite.
z49XjWjCqb.claimed_gains: Independent SFT on Qwen3.5-27B yields absolute gains over the initial model of 1.11%, 9.25%, 0.86%, and 2.33% on General Avg, BFCL Multi-turn, Tau2Bench three-domain Overall, and SWE-bench Lite, and 10.82%, 19.75%, 7.50%, and 8.00% over the best public-data baselines.

9nKhfJAHCH.one_liner: Co-evolves terminal agents with executable environments via a Discover-Shape-Evolve training loop.
9nKhfJAHCH.problem: Static executable terminal environments drift out of alignment with an improving agent as tasks become redundant and new capability bottlenecks appear.
9nKhfJAHCH.method: EvoTerminal runs a recurring Discover-Shape-Evolve loop that identifies the learner's behavioral frontier from feedback, reallocates practice across capabilities while calibrating difficulty, and instantiates target environments preserving the learning objective. The loop supports both model and harness adaptation.
9nKhfJAHCH.key_idea: Iteratively identifies an agent's behavioral frontier from feedback to reallocate capability practice, calibrate difficulty, and generate updated executable terminal environments.
9nKhfJAHCH.evidence: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (further details truncated in abstract).

2j0eUVr8bk.one_liner: Regularizes MLLM cross-modal attention on decisive tokens using gradient-based visual credits during RL.
2j0eUVr8bk.problem: Outcome-only reinforcement learning in multimodal LLMs leaves cross-modal attention unaligned on spatially decisive tokens such as coordinates.
2j0eUVr8bk.method: VISTA (Visual-credit Induced Self-attention Target Alignment) derives gradient-based visual credits to build target attention distributions specifically on decisive generation tokens. It selectively regularizes cross-modal attention toward these intrinsic targets within policy optimization.
2j0eUVr8bk.key_idea: Computes gradient-based visual credits to construct intrinsic attention targets that selectively regularize cross-modal attention on decisive tokens during RL.
2j0eUVr8bk.evidence: Evaluated on 3B and 7B MLLMs across visual grounding benchmarks (including LISA-G) and multimodal reasoning benchmarks, compared against InternVL2.5-38B.
2j0eUVr8bk.claimed_gains: Lifts 3B grounding accuracy from 68.5% to 70.3% and 7B from 69.8% to 72.1% (+4.3 and +4.8 on LISA-G), reaching 54.7% average on multimodal reasoning among 7B models.

wlVGQuzR0R.one_liner: Trains a single video MLLM to route between generation and retrieval via counterfactual RL.
wlVGQuzR0R.problem: Long-form video understanding systems either rely on one evidence acquisition strategy or separate routing into external modules decoupled from policy optimization.
wlVGQuzR0R.method: Route2Learn trains a single video MLLM in two stages: first executing both generation-based and retrieval-based strategies per query with rejection-sampled SFT trajectories, then applying Counterfactual Routing Policy Optimization (CRPO). CRPO optimizes routing from factual-versus-counterfactual outcome differences while decoupling advantages for tool selection and answer generation.
wlVGQuzR0R.key_idea: Optimizes native query-adaptive routing between generation and retrieval using factual-counterfactual rollout outcome differences and decoupled tool/answer advantages.

gA7iwrs6QN.one_liner: Reconstructs hidden people around corners from wall light via uncertainty-calibrated multiscale routing and hypothesis refinement.
gA7iwrs6QN.problem: Reconstructing a person hidden beyond an L-shaped corner from steady flashlight wall reflections suffers from severe attenuation, spatial mixing, noise, and structural ambiguity.
gA7iwrs6QN.method: LUMEN combines Path-Aware Calibrated Evidence Routing (PACER) with Evidence-Conditioned Hypothesis Optimization (ECHO). PACER estimates cue reliability under three-bounce diffuse reflection and routes multiscale evidence, while ECHO couples global structural hypothesis selection with progressive refinement conditioned on that evidence.
gA7iwrs6QN.key_idea: Estimates reliability of three-bounce wall cues for multiscale evidence routing and conditions global hypothesis selection and progressive refinement on it.
gA7iwrs6QN.evidence: Evaluated in an L-shaped corner hidden-human reconstruction setup using an ordinary camera and steady flashlight illumination (dataset details truncated in abstract).

MWgRLRwOWd.one_liner: Consolidates 13 public sources into MaliciousSkillBench, a deduplicated benchmark for malicious agent skill detection.
MWgRLRwOWd.problem: Existing malicious agent skill datasets are fragmented across formats and overlap across sources, inflating scale and leaking related artifacts across train-test splits.
MWgRLRwOWd.method: MaliciousSkillBench recovers artifact-level skills from 13 frozen public sources (11 yielding eligible malicious artifacts) and applies canonicalization, deduplication, structural family clustering, and conflict filtering with provenance tracking. It comprises 9,740 skills (7,505 malicious, 2,235 benign) mapped to 11 attack categories and evaluates cross-source generalization.
MWgRLRwOWd.key_idea: Canonicalizes, deduplicates, and structurally clusters agent skills across 13 public sources to benchmark malicious skill detection under held-out source splits.
MWgRLRwOWd.evidence: Evaluates sparse text baselines and a fine-tuned ModernBERT encoder on random versus leave-source-out splits over 9,740 skills.
MWgRLRwOWd.claimed_gains: When holding out whole sources on static primary-instruction text, the strongest sparse baseline drops from 0.932 to 0.665 Macro-F1, and fine-tuned ModernBERT drops from 0.964 to 0.734.

rziPqLPybX.one_liner: Factors out shared orthogonal drift via Procrustes alignment to regularize continual vision-language learning.
rziPqLPybX.problem: Continual learning regularizers for contrastive vision-language models penalize all representation drift, even though nearly half is retrieval-preserving shared orthogonal rotation.
rziPqLPybX.method: Decomposed Relative Geometry Preservation (Decomp-RGP) removes shared orthogonal transformations via closed-form Procrustes alignment, then decomposes residual drift into visual deformation, textual deformation, and cross-modal orthogonal alignment mismatch. A budget-based adaptive weighting scheme balances these three terms during fine-tuning.
rziPqLPybX.key_idea: Applies closed-form Procrustes alignment to factor out shared orthogonal drift and adaptively penalizes visual, textual, and cross-modal residual deformations.
rziPqLPybX.evidence: Evaluated on a seven-task continual image-text retrieval sequence and zero-shot retention across multiple CLIP backbones.
rziPqLPybX.claimed_gains: Improves Mean R@1 by 5.32% over the strongest baseline across seven image-text retrieval tasks.

yPJJ9o4Uey.one_liner: Adapts pre-trained virtual screening models to allosteric sites via multi-instance parameter-efficient tuning.
yPJJ9o4Uey.problem: Virtual screening models assume known orthosteric pockets, whereas allosteric sites are often unknown, conformation-dependent, and data-scarce.
yPJJ9o4Uey.method: AlloMIT plugs parameter-efficient tuning modules into pre-trained virtual screening alignment models and represents each protein as a bag of candidate pockets trained via weak multi-instance supervision without pocket annotations. Its Contextual Sparse Pocket Aggregation (CSPA) module models ligand-dependent pocket interactions and aggregates pocket scores sparsely.
yPJJ9o4Uey.key_idea: Treats proteins as candidate-pocket bags for parameter-efficient multi-instance tuning with ligand-conditioned sparse pocket aggregation.

KAvPoroQnT.one_liner: Diagnoses vision foundation model vulnerability on high-fidelity forgeries via Critical Optimization Radius.
KAvPoroQnT.problem: It is unclear whether general-purpose Vision Foundation Models retain transferable forensic cues needed to detect high-fidelity deepfakes.
KAvPoroQnT.method: The authors identify Optimization Collapse, where linear probes on frozen VFM features drop to chance under small adversarial parameter perturbations, and define the Critical Optimization Radius (COR) to quantify it. They link COR theoretically and empirically to the Gradient Signal-to-Noise Ratio (GSNR) and perform layer-wise analysis.
KAvPoroQnT.key_idea: Measures the adversarial parameter-perturbation radius at which frozen-VFM linear probes collapse to chance (COR) and links it to layer-wise GSNR.
KAvPoroQnT.evidence: Theoretical analysis relating COR to GSNR, plus cross-manipulation, within-manipulation interpolation, and layer-wise empirical studies on frozen VFM representations.

XuvWNrQ01K.one_liner: Continuously learns discriminative representations across batches to enable pixel-space one-step Drifting Models.
XuvWNrQ01K.problem: One-step Drifting Models perform poorly in pixel space and rely on pretrained feature spaces for reasons not previously explained.
XuvWNrQ01K.method: The authors trace drifting performance to the discriminative geometry governing kernel density estimation sample weighting and introduce persistent representation learning to continually update discriminative features alongside the evolving generator. They also prove a current-step gradient equivalence between KDE ratio loss and drift regression loss, motivating velocity clipping.
XuvWNrQ01K.key_idea: Continuously updates a discriminative feature space across batches to shape KDE-based drifting fields, backed by a gradient equivalence to density-ratio optimization.
XuvWNrQ01K.evidence: Theoretical gradient equivalence proof and image generation experiments on SVHN, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 from pixels and with adapted pretrained encoders.
XuvWNrQ01K.claimed_gains: Reduces FID by approximately 81-95% over original pixel-space Drifting Models on SVHN, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 without pretrained encoders.

pBt5wdwAPj.one_liner: Evaluates frozen vision models by predicting complete human scene-memory report distributions from visual similarity.
pBt5wdwAPj.problem: Visual working memory models typically score only accuracy or error magnitude, discarding which specific scene a person mistakenly reports.
pBt5wdwAPj.method: PRISM predicts full scene-memory report distributions from target-candidate visual similarity via three components: PRISM-Eval isolates frozen vision model contributions beyond six fixed image descriptors, PRISM-Channel embeds visual evidence in a precision-and-guessing cognitive model, and CCGD learns a compact combination of frozen model similarities.
pBt5wdwAPj.key_idea: Maps target-candidate similarities from frozen vision models through a memory precision-and-guessing channel to predict complete human scene-report distributions.
pBt5wdwAPj.evidence: Evaluated on two continuous-report datasets (including Scene Wheels), an independent memory transfer task, and independent EEG alignment.

hbEJ10jEL7.one_liner: Adapts per-objective regularization from train-held-out reward gaps to prevent differential overoptimization in multi-objective alignment.
hbEJ10jEL7.problem: Scalarizing heterogeneous rewards under a single shared KL budget causes overoptimization to concentrate unevenly on the most hackable objective.
hbEJ10jEL7.method: The authors formalize Differential Overoptimization and derive a closed-form allocation law linking each objective's collapse point to its hackability and train-held-out gap. They propose GAPOR (Gap-Adaptive Per-Objective Regularization), a per-objective adaptive regularizer with provable shrinkage, rebalancing, and bounded-gain closed-loop convergence.
hbEJ10jEL7.key_idea: Monitors each objective's train-held-out reward gap to adaptively regularize individual objectives instead of using one global KL budget.
hbEJ10jEL7.evidence: Theoretical convergence and allocation-law analysis, exact optimizer simulations, and multi-objective alignment experiments across multiple LLM families with independent gold evaluation.

PcY9mhQZT2.one_liner: Trains one shared contextual representation per modality for contrastive understanding, cross-modal conditioning, and continuous-flow generation.
PcY9mhQZT2.problem: Multimodal models typically separate understanding and generation into distinct representation spaces under the assumption that their objectives conflict.
PcY9mhQZT2.method: CoRe jointly shapes a single contextual representation per modality using both understanding and continuous-flow generation objectives. That shared representation is read for understanding, conditions generation of the other modality, and serves directly as the continuous space in which images and text are generated.
PcY9mhQZT2.key_idea: Jointly trains one contextual representation per modality to serve simultaneously as the understanding readout, cross-modal condition, and continuous-flow generation space.
PcY9mhQZT2.evidence: 383M-parameter model trained from scratch on CC12M, evaluated on global understanding, semantic segmentation probes, and COCO-30K generation against contrastive-only and frozen-representation baselines.
PcY9mhQZT2.claimed_gains: Reaches COCO-30K FID 10.10 with 383M parameters trained from scratch on CC12M while matching a contrastive-only model in global understanding.
